You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

lines.text: From: Victoria S. Andersen (vandersen@whitfieldcrane.com)
To: Nathan J. Reeves (nreeves@whitfieldcrane.com)
Subject: RE: Polaris / Trident — TSA Markup Assignment — Specialty Coatings
Divestiture
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable
MIME-Version: 1.0
Nathan,
Caldwell Briggs & Foley (Tom Graziano's team =E2=80=94 his associate Priya Ve=
nkatesh circulated) sent over Trident's first draft of the Transition Service=
s Agreement yesterday evening. I've done a quick initial skim but haven't had=
time to go through it with a fine-tooth comb =E2=80=94 that's where you come=
in.
For context, this is the TSA contemplated by Section 7.12 of the executed Ass=
et Purchase Agreement dated March 14, 2025, between Polaris Industrial Holdin=
gs, Inc. (as Seller and Service Provider) and Trident Manufacturing Group, In=
c. (as Buyer and Service Recipient) for the divestiture of the Specialty Coat=
ings Division. Expected closing is June 2, 2025, which means we need to turn =
around a comprehensive markup by end of next week at the latest. Sharon Petro=
sian wants to see our redline before it goes out to Caldwell Briggs, so we ca=
n't let this slip.
**General Assignment**
I need you to do a full-document markup of the draft TSA =E2=80=94 it runs ab=
out 48 pages =E2=80=94 against two key benchmarks: (1) the Polaris TSA Playbo=
ok (last updated January 15, 2025) and (2) the relevant provisions of the exe=
cuted APA, particularly Section 7.12 and Exhibit H.
I'm looking for two deliverables:
(a) A redlined markup of the draft with marginal comments explaining each pro=
posed change. For each comment, include the basis for the change, the risk to=
Polaris if the language remains unchanged, and whether it's a firm position =
or one where we have room to negotiate.
(b) A cover memo to me summarizing all identified deviations, organized by pr=
iority tier:
- **Critical** =E2=80=94 Direct conflicts with the executed APA that must =
be corrected
- **Significant** =E2=80=94 Major deviations from the Polaris playbook
- **Minor** =E2=80=94 Negotiation preferences and cleanup items
I'm attaching (or forwarding separately if the file sizes give us trouble) th=
ree documents: the Trident draft TSA (`trident-draft-tsa.docx`), the Polaris =
TSA Playbook (`polaris-tsa-playbook.docx`), and relevant APA excerpts (`apa-e=
xcerpts.docx`). You should already have the full executed APA in the deal fol=
der, but the excerpted version isolates the TSA-relevant provisions =E2=80=94=
Section 7.12, Exhibit H, and the relevant definitions =E2=80=94 so it should=
be easier to work from.
**High-Priority Areas =E2=80=94 Liability and Damages**
On my initial skim, the liability cap language looked off. It appeared to ref=
erence a percentage of total fees rather than the trailing 12-month fee formu=
lation required by APA Section 7.12(d). I need you to be particularly careful=
here. Run the actual numbers =E2=80=94 quantify Polaris's exposure under the=
draft language versus the APA-mandated cap so we can show the delta clearly.=
If there's a material discrepancy, this is a must-fix.
Also scrutinize the consequential damages waiver. I recall seeing language th=
at may only run one way =E2=80=94 i.e., waiving Polaris's ability to recover =
consequential damages from Trident but not the reverse. If that's the case, i=
t's unacceptable under the playbook. The waiver needs to be mutual. Flag it p=
rominently.
**High-Priority Areas =E2=80=94 IP and Data Ownership**
The draft appears to contain some kind of license grant to Trident covering P=
olaris's tools, methodologies, and know-how. This is a non-starter. The Polar=
is playbook takes a firm no-license position, and for good reason =E2=80=94 P=
olaris's operational IP, including proprietary processes used across all four=
divisions (not just Specialty Coatings), cannot be licensed out through a TS=
A. Delete any such license and replace it with clear language reserving all P=
olaris IP. Both David Okafor and Sharon Petrosian have flagged IP leakage as =
a top concern for the board, so this needs to be airtight.
**High-Priority Areas =E2=80=94 Monterrey Cross-Border Issues**
This one deserves special attention. The Monterrey, Mexico manufacturing faci=
lity (Avenida Industrial 1450, Parque Industrial Monterrey, Monterrey, Nuevo =
Le=C3=B3n, C.P. 64000, Mexico) raises a couple of issues I did not see addres=
sed in the draft.
First, the Monterrey facility operates under Mexico's IMMEX program =E2=80=94=
the maquiladora/manufacturing export regime. The draft TSA does not appear t=
o address which party is responsible for maintaining the IMMEX certification =
during the transition period. This is not a trivial gap. Loss or suspension o=
f the IMMEX certification could have significant customs duty and tax consequ=
ences for the carved-out business. I need you to flag any cross-border issues=
and propose language addressing IMMEX program compliance responsibilities =
=E2=80=94 who maintains the certification, who bears the cost, what happens i=
f the certification is jeopardized, and what the notification obligations loo=
k like.
Second, Polaris's HR and payroll services under the TSA will involve processi=
ng personal data of the approximately 300+ Mexican employees at the Monterrey=
facility, which implicates Mexico's Federal Law on Protection of Personal Da=
ta Held by Private Parties (the "LFPDPPP"). The draft TSA references only U.S=
. data privacy law and does not address the LFPDPPP's requirements for data p=
rocessing agreements and cross-border data transfer consent mechanisms. I nee=
d you to propose appropriate provisions =E2=80=94 potentially a data processi=
ng addendum or at minimum specific TSA provisions =E2=80=94 to ensure Polaris=
is not exposed to liability for non-compliant processing of Mexican employee=
personal data. If you need to consult with the firm's Latin America practice=
group for the precise LFPDPPP requirements, reach out to them, but in the me=
antime flag the issue clearly in both the markup and the memo with your best =
proposed language. Don't leave it as a placeholder =E2=80=94 give me somethin=
g substantive to react to.
**Additional Areas to Review Carefully**
This is not exhaustive, but based on my quick skim and general TSA experience=
, I want you to focus on the following. I'm not giving you the answers =E2=80=
=94 I expect you to identify the specific problems and propose solutions:
- **Term and renewal provisions:** Check that the term is consistent with the=
APA's 18-month maximum. I recall seeing something about automatic renewals t=
hat didn't look right.
- **Termination notice periods:** Verify consistency with APA Section 7.12(c)=
's 90-day notice requirement.
- **Fee schedules:** Run the numbers on each service category to confirm the =
markups are within the APA Section 7.12(b) cap of 10%. Cross-check each line =
item against the Exhibit H cost estimates.
- **Service standard:** Compare against the playbook's "substantially consist=
ent" formulation. Any "best efforts" or "best practices" language needs to be=
flagged.
- **Staffing/personnel provisions:** Confirm Polaris retains discretion over =
staffing per the playbook. Think about what's reasonable here =E2=80=94 there=
may be room for some notice obligation to Trident, but we need to protect Po=
laris's operational flexibility.
- **Governing law and dispute resolution:** Check whether it matches the play=
book (Pennsylvania law, AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh).
- **Audit rights:** Review frequency, cost allocation, and notice period.
- **Missing provisions:** Cross-reference the draft against the playbook to i=
dentify any standard playbook provisions that are entirely absent from the dr=
aft. I'm thinking specifically of things like non-solicitation, termination a=
ssistance, change order procedure, payment terms, force majeure as a terminat=
ion trigger, fee escalation mechanics, and insurance requirements. If it's in=
the playbook and not in the draft, I want to know about it.
**Guidance on Approach and Tone**
A few strategic points to keep in mind as you work through this:
For anything that directly conflicts with the executed APA, mark it as a "mus=
t-change." These are not negotiable =E2=80=94 the APA is a binding agreement =
and the TSA must conform. Full stop.
For playbook deviations that don't conflict with the APA, use your judgment o=
n prioritization. Some are firm positions (e.g., mutual consequential damages=
waiver, no IP license), others may have room for compromise. For example, on=
key personnel =E2=80=94 some notice obligation to Trident before reassigning=
dedicated personnel may be reasonable even if the playbook prefers sole disc=
retion. Tell me where you think we have flexibility and where we don't.
One other thing: even where a provision might arguably benefit Polaris =E2=80=
=94 for instance, if a fee is miscalculated in our favor =E2=80=94 flag and c=
orrect it. Maintaining credibility and APA compliance is more important than =
a short-term fee advantage. Tom Graziano is a reasonable counterpart, and I e=
xpect most issues can be resolved in one or two rounds of markup, but we need=
to come in with a well-supported initial position.
Keep in mind that Polaris is providing these services as an accommodation to =
facilitate the divestiture, not as a long-term service business. The TSA shou=
ld be structured to incentivize Trident to migrate off Polaris's systems as q=
uickly as possible. If you see provisions that create perverse incentives =E2=
=80=94 e.g., below-market pricing with no escalation, or renewal mechanisms t=
hat allow Trident to stay on indefinitely =E2=80=94 flag them.
**Logistics**
I need the redline and cover memo on my desk by close of business Friday, May=
9. I'll review over the weekend and we can discuss Monday morning before sen=
ding to Sharon for client approval.
I have a call with Sharon on Thursday, May 1, to discuss the status of the TS=
A negotiations and other pre-closing workstreams. If you identify anything tr=
uly alarming in your initial review =E2=80=94 APA conflicts that could affect=
closing, IP issues that the board needs to know about, anything of that magn=
itude =E2=80=94 flag it to me before that call so I'm not caught off guard.
Bill to the standard Polaris/Specialty Coatings Divestiture matter number.
Let me know if you have questions after you've had a chance to dig in.
Thanks,
Victoria

This document is protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work-product doctrine. It contains the legal strategies, negotiation positions, and confidential assessments of Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. and its counsel. Distribution is strictly limited to authorized personnel. Any unauthorized disclosure, copying, or distribution is prohibited and may constitute a waiver of applicable privileges.

**Maintained by:** Legal Department, Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc., 1200 Commonwealth Avenue, Suite 3000, Pittsburgh, PA 15222

**Approved by:** Sharon M. Petrosian, General Counsel

**Last Updated:** January 15, 2025

**Version:** 4.2

**Distribution:** Limited to Polaris Legal Department, CFO (David K. Okafor), CEO (Margaret R. Lindstrom), and outside counsel (Whitfield & Crane LLP, 600 Grant Street, Suite 4800, Pittsburgh, PA 15219; Lead Partner: Victoria S. Andersen)

This Playbook sets forth Polaris\'s preferred and fallback positions for any Transition Services Agreement in which Polaris acts as Service Provider following a divestiture. All positions should be adapted to the specific transaction and governing purchase agreement. Positions marked **\"Target\"** represent Polaris\'s opening/preferred position. Positions marked **\"Fallback\"** represent the maximum acceptable concession, below which escalation to the General Counsel is required.

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[Section 1: Purpose and Scope of Playbook]{.underline}**

Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. is a diversified industrial conglomerate incorporated in Delaware, with approximately \$3.2 billion in annual revenue across four operating divisions: Advanced Materials, Specialty Coatings, Precision Components, and Industrial Automation. Polaris is headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and maintains domestic and international operations including a manufacturing facility in Monterrey, Mexico.

Divestitures of individual business units frequently require Polaris to provide post-closing transition services to buyers. This need arises because Polaris\'s shared-services infrastructure --- encompassing IT, HR/Payroll, Finance/Accounting, Supply Chain/Procurement, Regulatory/EHS, and Treasury/Tax functions --- supports multiple divisions simultaneously through common personnel and integrated systems. Approximately 100 full-time equivalents across these service categories typically support any single division alongside other Polaris businesses. These personnel remain Polaris employees after closing, necessitating a Transition Services Agreement under which Polaris continues to perform certain functions on behalf of the buyer for a defined transition period.

The purpose of this Playbook is to protect Polaris\'s interests as Service Provider by:

> • **(a)** Limiting liability exposure arising from the provision of transition services;
>
> • **(b)** Preserving Polaris\'s operational flexibility to manage its own workforce and systems;
>
> • **(c)** Protecting Polaris\'s proprietary intellectual property, systems, and know-how;
>
> • **(d)** Ensuring adequate compensation for the administrative burden and resource diversion inherent in service delivery; and
>
> • **(e)** Maintaining compliance with the terms and constraints set forth in the governing purchase agreement.

This Playbook should always be read in conjunction with the applicable Asset Purchase Agreement (or Stock Purchase Agreement, as applicable). Where the APA mandates specific TSA terms --- including service standard, term, fee cap, or liability structure --- the APA controls and those terms are not subject to further negotiation in the TSA. The Playbook serves as the benchmark against which any buyer\'s draft TSA is evaluated, and any deviation from the positions stated herein should be flagged, analyzed, and escalated as appropriate.

**[Section 2: Service Standard]{.underline}**

**[2.1 Standard of Performance]{.underline}**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Services shall be provided *\"in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality provided to the Business during the twelve (12) months prior to the Closing Date.\"* No obligation to exceed historical service levels. No obligation to prioritize Service Recipient over Polaris\'s own internal business needs.

  **Fallback**                        Add *\"using commercially reasonable efforts\"* after *\"substantially consistent\"* language. This is the maximum concession.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • **Lookback Period:** The lookback period is twelve (12) months prior to the Closing Date. Do not accept a 24-month or longer lookback period. A longer lookback may capture atypical service levels (e.g., pre-pandemic staffing, special project surges) that are not representative of current operations.
>
> • **\"Substantially Consistent\" Language:** The operative standard is *\"substantially consistent with,\"* which permits reasonable variation. Reject language such as *\"equal to or better than,\"* *\"at least equal to,\"* or *\"no less favorable than.\"* These formulations impose a floor that ratchets upward and does not permit any reduction or variation, however reasonable.
>
> • **Reject \"Best Practices\" and Similar Standards:** References to *\"industry best practices,\"* *\"commercially reasonable best efforts,\"* or other aspirational benchmarks must be rejected. These terms are undefined, subjective, invite disputes, and impose a standard that may materially exceed what Polaris historically provided to the divested business. Polaris is not a third-party service provider competing for business --- it is providing transitional support as an accommodation.
>
> • **Not a Guarantor:** Service Provider\'s obligation is limited to making available the same general type and level of resources as historically deployed. Service Provider does not guarantee specific outcomes, results, or service levels beyond what was historically provided.
>
> • **APA Precedence:** If the APA specifies a service standard (e.g., in the TSA covenant section or an exhibit), that APA standard controls and the TSA cannot impose a more stringent requirement.

**[2.2 Exclusions from Service Obligation]{.underline}**

Service Provider has no obligation to:

> • **(a)** Provide services not described in the applicable Service Schedules;
>
> • **(b)** Hire additional personnel or acquire additional resources beyond those in place as of the Closing Date;
>
> • **(c)** Provide services that would violate applicable law or regulation;
>
> • **(d)** Provide services that would breach any third-party agreement to which Polaris is a party (including software licenses, vendor contracts, or confidentiality agreements);
>
> • **(e)** Provide advice of any kind --- legal, tax, financial, or strategic.

Service Provider may modify the manner of delivering services to the extent such modifications are consistent with changes made to services provided to Polaris\'s own businesses (e.g., system upgrades, vendor changes, process improvements applied company-wide).

**[Section 3: Term and Termination]{.underline}**

**[3.1 Maximum Term]{.underline}**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Fixed term not to exceed **18 months** from the Closing Date. Hard stop. No automatic renewal. Extensions require: (i) mutual written agreement, (ii) pricing at cost-plus-15%, (iii) maximum extension of 6 months (total possible term: 24 months only upon mutual agreement).

  **Fallback**                        Mutual written extension option at cost-plus-10% (minimum). Never accept automatic renewals.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • The 18-month maximum is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12 in standard Polaris deals. The TSA cannot exceed the APA-mandated term.
>
> • **Automatic renewal provisions are strictly prohibited.** Automatic renewals create open-ended service obligations, may violate APA term caps, deprive Polaris of the ability to reallocate resources to its remaining businesses, and eliminate Polaris\'s leverage to negotiate extension pricing.
>
> • Extension pricing at cost-plus-15% reflects the additional administrative burden, resource diversion, and opportunity cost of extended service delivery beyond the original contemplated term.

**[3.2 Termination of Individual Services]{.underline}**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Either party may terminate any individual Service upon **90 days\'** prior written notice.

  **Fallback**                        90 days for Service Recipient termination; 60 days for Service Provider termination upon Service Recipient material breach. Service Recipient may terminate on 30 days\' notice if the applicable function has been fully migrated.
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The 90-day notice period is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12(c). Do not accept termination notice periods longer than 90 days, as longer periods lock Polaris into service obligations even when continued provision is inefficient or undesirable.

**[3.3 Termination for Cause]{.underline}**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Either party may terminate the entire TSA upon material breach if the breaching party fails to cure within **30 days** of receiving written notice. Service Provider may terminate immediately (no cure period) upon: (i) Service Recipient insolvency or bankruptcy, (ii) failure to pay undisputed invoices for more than 60 days past due, or (iii) conduct creating material legal, regulatory, or reputational risk for Polaris.

  **Fallback**                        Accept 45-day cure period. Maintain immediate termination rights for insolvency and non-payment.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**[3.4 Termination Assistance / Wind-Down]{.underline}**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Upon expiration or termination of any Service, Service Provider shall provide reasonable termination assistance for a period not to exceed **60 days** at **cost-plus-15%**. Assistance includes: knowledge transfer, data migration support, cooperation with replacement providers, and transition documentation. No obligation to provide termination assistance if Service Recipient has outstanding unpaid invoices.

  **Fallback**                        Extend termination assistance period to 90 days maximum. Accept cost-plus-10% as absolute floor.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Critical Note:** The TSA must include termination assistance provisions. A TSA that is silent on wind-down obligations creates ambiguity regarding Polaris\'s post-termination cooperation obligations and exposes Polaris to claims that implied duties of good faith require indefinite assistance. Affirmatively negotiating a defined, compensated wind-down period protects Polaris by establishing clear boundaries.

**[Section 4: Service Fees and Payment]{.underline}**

**[4.1 Fee Calculation Methodology]{.underline}**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          All service fees calculated on a **cost-plus-10%** basis: fully-loaded cost (direct labor, allocated overhead, system costs, out-of-pocket expenses) plus a **uniform 10% markup** across all service categories.

  **Fallback**                        Accept cost-plus-7% or cost-plus-8% if buyer pushes back. Never accept a markup below cost-plus-5%.
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • The cost-plus-10% cap is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12(b). All fee calculations must be verified for compliance with this APA-mandated ceiling.
>
> • The 10% markup applies **uniformly** to all service categories. There shall be no service category that carries a different (higher or lower) markup percentage. Any deviation from uniform pricing must be flagged.
>
> • Each Service Schedule must include: (i) base cost components, (ii) estimated monthly cost, (iii) markup percentage, and (iv) resulting monthly fee. A consolidated Fee Schedule should be attached as an exhibit.

**[4.2 Fee Escalation]{.underline}**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Annual escalation (on each anniversary of Closing) by the greater of **(a) 3%** or **(b) CPI-U** for the trailing 12-month period. Additional escalation upon an \"Escalation Event\" (material cost increase due to changes in law/regulation/vendor pricing, or Service Recipient request for material volume/scope increase).

  **Fallback**                        Accept CPI-U only (no 3% floor). Maintain Escalation Event provision.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**[4.3 Payment Terms]{.underline}**

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Monthly invoicing within 15 business days after month-end. Payment due **Net 30** from date of invoice. Late interest at the lesser of **1.5% per month** or maximum rate permitted by law. Undisputed portions must be paid regardless of disputes over other portions.

  **Fallback**                        Accept Net 45 as maximum. Interest at 1.0%/month as floor.
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Critical Note:** Never accept vague payment language such as *\"payment within a commercially reasonable time\"* or *\"payment to be made promptly.\"* Specific payment terms are essential for cash flow management and enforcement. Vague formulations are unenforceable as a practical matter and create unnecessary disputes.

**[4.4 Change Orders]{.underline}**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Any request for out-of-scope services, material volume increase, or material scope change requires a **written change order** signed by authorized representatives of both parties. Change order pricing: **cost-plus-15%**. Acceptance at Service Provider\'s **sole discretion**. No obligation to perform until change order is fully executed and any required advance payment received.

  **Fallback**                        Accept cost-plus-10% for change orders. Maintain written change order requirement, dual signature, and Service Provider discretion.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Critical Note:** The TSA must include a formal change order procedure. Without one, Service Recipient can expand scope through informal requests and then argue that expanded services are covered under the existing fee structure. A documented change order process protects Polaris against scope creep and ensures compensation for incremental burden.

**[Section 5: Liability and Indemnification]{.underline}**

**[5.1 Limitation of Liability --- Aggregate Cap]{.underline}**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Service Provider\'s aggregate liability shall not exceed total fees actually paid during the **trailing twelve (12) month period** preceding the date on which the claim first arose.

  **Fallback**                        **APA-mandated; not subject to negotiation.** APA Section 7.12(d) specifies the trailing 12-month fee cap. The TSA must conform.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Key Negotiation Points --- Illustrative Exposure Analysis:**

The distinction between a trailing 12-month fee cap and a total-fees (or total-fee-multiple) cap is significant. Using representative assumptions:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Cap Formulation**                  **Calculation**                **Approximate Exposure**
  ------------------------------------ ------------------------------ --------------------------
  Trailing 12-month fees               \~\$1,122,000/month × 12       **\~\$13,464,000**

  200% of total fees (18-month term)   \~\$1,122,000/month × 18 × 2   **\~\$40,392,000**
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The total-fees formulation creates approximately three times the exposure of the trailing 12-month cap. Reject any liability cap based on total fees paid over the entire term, any multiple thereof, or any fixed dollar amount that exceeds the trailing 12-month fee calculation. The trailing 12-month structure is appropriately calibrated to the ongoing relationship and reflects the APA mandate.

**[5.2 Consequential Damages Waiver]{.underline}**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          **MUTUAL** waiver of all consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, and indirect damages (including lost profits, lost revenue, loss of business opportunity, and diminution in value). Exceptions: (i) breaches of confidentiality, (ii) IP infringement, (iii) third-party claim indemnification.

  **Fallback**                        Firm position. Accept narrow additional carve-outs (willful misconduct, fraud). **Never accept a non-mutual waiver.**
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Critical Note:** The waiver must be **mutual** --- both parties waive claims against the other. A unilateral waiver (where only Service Recipient waives) is insufficient because it leaves Service Provider exposed to potentially unlimited consequential damages claims. As service provider, Polaris\'s consequential damages exposure (e.g., claims for business interruption, lost contracts, or supply chain disruption) could vastly exceed the TSA fee value. The mutual waiver limits both parties to direct damages.

**[5.3 Indemnification]{.underline}**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          Service Recipient indemnifies Service Provider against all third-party claims arising from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance upon Services, except to the extent caused by Service Provider\'s **gross negligence or willful misconduct**. Service Provider\'s indemnification limited to third-party claims arising from its gross negligence or willful misconduct. All indemnification subject to the aggregate cap in Section 5.1.

  **Fallback**                        Accept proportionate fault standard. Maintain gross negligence/willful misconduct threshold for Service Provider indemnification.
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**[Section 6: Intellectual Property and Data]{.underline}**

**[6.1 IP Ownership]{.underline}**

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                      **Position**
  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Target**                          All Service Provider IP (proprietary technology, tools, methodologies, templates, software, systems, know-how, and processes) remains the **sole and exclusive property** of Service Provider. **No license, sublicense, right, or interest** granted to Service Recipient. Access ceases immediately upon expiration or termination.

  **Fallback**                        **Firm position. No license grant is acceptable.** If buyer requires specific tools post-transition, address through a separate, independently negotiated license agreement with appropriate restrictions and compensation.
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • Reject any license grant --- including non-exclusive, limited, or term-limited licenses --- to Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, templates, or know-how.
>
> • **Specifically reject** language granting *\"perpetual,\" \"irrevocable,\"* or *\"royalty-free\"* licenses. Such language permanently divests Polaris of exclusive control over its proprietary operational IP.
>
> • Service Recipient receives no right to use, access, copy, modify, reverse engineer, or create derivative works of any Service Provider IP outside of receiving the Services during the Term.
>

**[EXCERPTS FROM EXECUTED ASSET PURCHASE AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**ASSET PURCHASE AGREEMENT**

**dated as of March 14, 2025**

**by and between**

**POLARIS INDUSTRIAL HOLDINGS, INC.**

**and**

**TRIDENT MANUFACTURING GROUP, INC.**

This document contains selected excerpts from the Asset Purchase Agreement dated as of March 14, 2025, by and between Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. and Trident Manufacturing Group, Inc. The complete Asset Purchase Agreement is approximately 180 pages. Only the provisions relevant to the Transition Services Agreement are reproduced herein. Sections, exhibits, and schedules not reproduced are indicated by bracketed editorial notations. Defined terms used but not defined in these excerpts have the meanings given to them in the full Asset Purchase Agreement.

**APA Execution Date: March 14, 2025**

**[PREAMBLE AND RECITALS (EXCERPT)]{.underline}**

This ASSET PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of March 14, 2025, by and between:

**POLARIS INDUSTRIAL HOLDINGS, INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal offices at 1200 Commonwealth Avenue, Suite 3000, Pittsburgh, PA 15222 (\"**Seller**\"),

and

**TRIDENT MANUFACTURING GROUP, INC.**, an Ohio corporation, with its principal offices at 800 Lakeside Drive, Suite 400, Cleveland, OH 44114 (\"**Buyer**\").

**RECITALS**

**WHEREAS:**

\(A\) Seller operates, among other businesses, the Specialty Coatings Division (as defined below), which is engaged in the development, manufacture, distribution, and sale of specialty industrial coatings and related products throughout the United States, Mexico, and internationally;

\(B\) Seller desires to sell, transfer, assign, convey, and deliver to Buyer, and Buyer desires to purchase, acquire, and accept from Seller, substantially all of the assets, properties, and rights of every kind and nature owned, leased, licensed, or used by Seller primarily in connection with the Specialty Coatings Division, and Buyer is willing to assume certain specified liabilities relating thereto, in each case subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein;

\(C\) The Board of Directors of each of Seller and Buyer has approved the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and has determined that such transactions are advisable and in the best interests of their respective stockholders; and

\(D\) Certain capitalized terms used in this Agreement are defined in Article I hereof.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements hereinafter set forth and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS (SELECTED DEFINITIONS)]{.underline}**

**[Section 1.1 --- Definitions]{.underline}**

*\[Note: Only definitions relevant to Section 7.12 and Exhibit H are excerpted below. The full Agreement contains approximately 142 defined terms.\]*

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

\"**Acquired Assets**\" means all of the assets, properties, and rights of every kind and nature, whether real, personal, or mixed, tangible or intangible, owned, leased, licensed, or used by Seller primarily in connection with the Business, including without limitation: (i) the Facilities; (ii) all machinery, equipment, tools, furniture, fixtures, supplies, vehicles, and other tangible personal property set forth on Schedule 2.1(a) or otherwise used primarily in the Business; (iii) all Inventory; (iv) all Transferred Intellectual Property; (v) all Assumed Contracts; (vi) all Permits; (vii) all books, records, and files, in whatever form or medium, to the extent primarily relating to the Business; and (viii) all goodwill associated with the Business. The term \"Acquired Assets\" is more fully defined in, and subject to the exclusions set forth in, Section 2.1 and Section 2.2 of this Agreement.

\"**Business**\" means the Specialty Coatings Division of Seller, including all operations, activities, and assets primarily related to the research, development, manufacture, formulation, marketing, distribution, and sale of specialty industrial coatings and related products, as conducted by Seller as of the date hereof and as of the Closing Date. For the avoidance of doubt, the term \"Business\" does not include Seller\'s Architectural Coatings Division, its Performance Polymers Division, or any other business unit or division of Seller other than the Specialty Coatings Division.

\"**Closing**\" means the closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, which shall take place in accordance with Section 3.2.

\"**Closing Date**\" means the date on which the Closing occurs, which the parties anticipate will be June 2, 2025, or such other date as the parties may mutually agree in writing; provided, however, that the Closing shall occur no later than the fifth (5th) Business Day following the satisfaction or waiver of all conditions to the obligations of the parties to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby (other than conditions that by their nature are to be satisfied at the Closing, but subject to the satisfaction or waiver of such conditions), unless otherwise agreed in writing by the parties.

\"**Facilities**\" means, collectively: (a) the manufacturing facility and related real property located at 4500 Industry Park Boulevard, Pittsburgh, PA 15205 (the \"**Pittsburgh Manufacturing Facility**\"); (b) the manufacturing facility and related real property located at 220 Pelham Road, Building C, Greenville, SC 29615 (the \"**Greenville Manufacturing Facility**\"); and (c) the manufacturing facility and related real property located at Avenida Industrial 1450, Parque Industrial Monterrey, Monterrey, Nuevo León, C.P. 64000, Mexico (the \"**Monterrey Facility**\").

\"**Fully-Loaded Cost**\" means, with respect to any Transition Service, the sum of: (a) direct labor costs (including base salary, wages, bonuses, commissions, and overtime) of personnel performing such Transition Service; (b) the employer portion of all payroll taxes and employee benefits (including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability, retirement plan contributions, and workers\' compensation insurance premiums) attributable to such personnel; (c) a reasonable allocation of overhead costs, including facilities costs, management and supervisory costs, and shared infrastructure costs, in each case allocated on a basis consistent with Seller\'s historical cost allocation methodology as applied to the Business during the twelve (12) months prior to the Closing Date; and (d) reasonable out-of-pocket costs and expenses incurred by Seller directly in connection with providing such Transition Service, including third-party software license fees, third-party service provider fees, telecommunications costs, and travel expenses. For purposes of calculating Fully-Loaded Cost, Seller shall not include any costs or expenses attributable to services or personnel that are not reasonably allocable to the Transition Service in question.

\"**IMMEX Program**\" means the Mexican Maquiladora and Export Services Industry Program (*Industria Manufacturera, Maquiladora y de Servicios de Exportación*) established under Mexico\'s Decree for the Promotion of the Manufacturing, Maquiladora and Export Services Industry, as amended from time to time, and all implementing rules, regulations, and official standards issued thereunder.

\"**Person**\" means an individual, corporation, partnership, joint venture, limited liability company, Governmental Authority, unincorporated organization, trust, association, or other entity.

\"**Purchase Price**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 3.1.

\"**Seller Note**\" means the promissory note in the principal amount of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000) to be issued by Buyer to Seller at the Closing, bearing interest at a rate per annum equal to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York plus three and one-half percent (3.50%), compounded monthly, maturing on the second (2nd) anniversary of the Closing Date, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit D.

\"**Shared Services Employees**\" means those employees of Seller listed on Schedule 4.12(b) who provide services to the Business but who also provide services to one or more other business units or divisions of Seller, and who will remain employees of Seller following the Closing. As of the date hereof, there are approximately one hundred (100) Shared Services Employees. For the avoidance of doubt, Shared Services Employees are not Transferred Employees.

\"**Specialty Coatings Division**\" means Seller\'s specialty coatings business unit, which is not a separate legal entity but is operated as a division of Seller and includes all personnel, assets, operations, and activities described in the definition of \"Business.\" For the avoidance of doubt, the Specialty Coatings Division is the Business.

\"**Transferred Employees**\" means those employees of Seller primarily dedicated to the Business who accept offers of employment from Buyer in accordance with Section 7.8. As of the date hereof, the parties anticipate that approximately one thousand one hundred eighty (1,180) employees of the approximately one thousand two hundred eighty (1,280) employees of the Specialty Coatings Division will be Transferred Employees. The final list of Transferred Employees shall be determined in accordance with the procedures set forth in Section 7.8(b).

\"**Transition Service**\" or \"**Transition Services**\" means the services to be provided by Seller (or its Affiliates) to Buyer (or its Affiliates) following the Closing pursuant to the Transition Services Agreement, as more particularly described in Exhibit H hereto.

\"**Transition Services Agreement**\" or \"**TSA**\" means the Transition Services Agreement to be entered into by Seller and Buyer at or prior to the Closing in accordance with Section 7.12, substantially in the form to be mutually agreed by the parties prior to the Closing Date.

*\[Remainder of Section 1.1 omitted. Approximately 128 additional defined terms are set forth in the full Agreement.\]*

**[EXCERPTED PROVISIONS FROM ARTICLE III --- PURCHASE PRICE]{.underline}**

*\[Article III of the Agreement addresses the Purchase Price, its components, the mechanics of the Closing, and post-closing adjustments. Section 3.1 is excerpted below for context.\]*

**[Section 3.1 --- Purchase Price]{.underline}**

The aggregate purchase price for the Acquired Assets shall be Four Hundred Eighty-Five Million Dollars (\$485,000,000) (the \"**Purchase Price**\"), consisting of:

> \(a\) Four Hundred Forty-Five Million Dollars (\$445,000,000) in cash (the \"**Cash Consideration**\"), payable by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account or accounts designated by Seller in writing at least three (3) Business Days prior to the Closing Date; and
>
> \(b\) the Seller Note in the principal amount of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), duly executed and delivered by Buyer to Seller at the Closing.

The Purchase Price shall be subject to customary post-closing adjustments for working capital, as set forth in Section 3.3. Any adjustment to the Purchase Price pursuant to Section 3.3 shall be made in cash and shall be paid by the applicable party within five (5) Business Days following final determination of the Closing Working Capital in accordance with the procedures set forth therein.

*\[Sections 3.2 through 3.5 omitted.\]*

**[EXCERPTED PROVISIONS FROM ARTICLE VII --- COVENANTS]{.underline}**

*\[Article VII of the Agreement contains covenants of the parties from signing through Closing and certain post-Closing covenants. Sections 7.1 through 7.11 address, among other things, conduct of the Business pending the Closing, access to information and properties, regulatory filings and approvals, certain employee matters, and other pre-Closing covenants, and are not reproduced herein. Section 7.12, which governs the Transition Services Agreement, is reproduced in full below. Sections 7.13 through 7.18 address non-competition and non-solicitation covenants, public announcements, tax matters, further assurances, and other post-Closing covenants, and are not reproduced herein.\]*

**[Section 7.12 --- Transition Services Agreement]{.underline}**

**Section 7.12(a) --- Obligation to Enter into TSA**

At or prior to the Closing, Seller and Buyer shall negotiate in good faith and enter into a Transition Services Agreement, on commercially reasonable terms and conditions, pursuant to which Seller shall provide, or cause to be provided, to Buyer (or its applicable Affiliates) the Transition Services described in Exhibit H hereto for a transition period following the Closing Date (the \"**Transition Period**\"). The purpose of the Transition Services Agreement is to facilitate an orderly transition of the Business from Seller to Buyer and to enable Buyer to establish independent operational capability with respect to the functions and services described in Exhibit H.

The Transition Period shall commence on the Closing Date and shall not exceed eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Maximum TSA Term**\"). Each individual Transition Service shall be provided for the period specified in Exhibit H with respect to such Transition Service, which period shall in no event exceed the Maximum TSA Term.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Transition Period shall expire no later than the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to extend the Transition Period for any individual Transition Service, provided that no such extension shall exceed an additional six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for any individual Transition Service. Any such extension shall be documented in a written amendment to the Transition Services Agreement executed by both parties. No automatic renewal or extension mechanism shall be included in the Transition Services Agreement.

The Transition Services shall be provided in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services were provided to the Business during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the Closing Date. Seller shall allocate sufficient resources and qualified personnel to provide the Transition Services in accordance with the foregoing standard throughout the Transition Period.

**Section 7.12(b) --- Service Fees**

All fees payable by Buyer to Seller under the Transition Services Agreement for the Transition Services (the \"**TSA Fees**\") shall be calculated on a cost-plus basis, reflecting the Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost (as defined in Section 1.1) of providing each Transition Service, plus a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost.

The estimated Fully-Loaded Cost and estimated monthly TSA Fees for each category of Transition Services are set forth in Exhibit H. Such estimates are based on Seller\'s actual cost experience for the twelve (12) months ended December 31, 2024, and shall be subject to adjustment in the Transition Services Agreement to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period, provided that any such adjustment shall be calculated in accordance with the Fully-Loaded Cost definition and shall not exceed the estimated amounts set forth in Exhibit H by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent.

In no event shall the markup applied to any category of Transition Service exceed ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost for such category. This limitation shall apply to each category of Transition Service individually and not solely on an aggregate or blended basis across all categories.

Any fees for services that are not described in Exhibit H but that are requested by Buyer and agreed to by Seller in writing (\"**Additional Services**\") shall be priced on terms to be mutually agreed by the parties, which pricing may include a markup in excess of ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with a good faith estimate of the Fully-Loaded Cost and proposed markup for any Additional Service prior to the commencement of such Additional Service.

**Section 7.12(c) --- Termination of Individual Services**

Buyer or Seller may terminate any individual Transition Service upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other party, specifying the Transition Service to be terminated and the effective date of such termination. Such notice shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 12.1 of this Agreement.

Upon termination of any individual Transition Service, Buyer\'s obligation to pay TSA Fees with respect to such terminated Transition Service shall cease as of the effective date of termination, subject to Buyer\'s obligation to pay all TSA Fees accrued through such effective date and to reimburse Seller for any non-cancelable costs or commitments that Seller incurred prior to receipt of the termination notice in reasonable reliance on the continuation of such Transition Service, provided that Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate such non-cancelable costs.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Transition Services Agreement provides for a notice period different from the ninety (90) day period specified in this Section 7.12(c), the notice period set forth in this Agreement shall control. The parties acknowledge and agree that this Section 7.12(c) establishes the minimum and maximum notice period applicable to the termination of individual Transition Services, and any provision in the Transition Services Agreement purporting to require a longer or shorter notice period shall be of no force or effect.

**Section 7.12(d) --- Limitation of Liability**

The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that the aggregate liability of the Service Provider (and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents) to the Service Recipient under or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, whether arising in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient to the Service Provider during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient (the \"**TSA Liability Cap**\").

For purposes of calculating the TSA Liability Cap during the first twelve (12) months of the Transition Period, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated based on the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient from the Closing Date through the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient. Thereafter, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated on a rolling twelve (12) month basis, measured from the date of assertion of the applicable claim and looking back twelve (12) months from such date.

The limitation set forth in this Section 7.12(d) shall not apply to:

> \(i\) claims arising from a party\'s fraud or willful misconduct;
>
> \(ii\) a party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations under the Transition Services Agreement; or
>
> \(iii\) a party\'s indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims arising out of the provision or receipt of Transition Services, to the extent such third-party claims result from the indemnifying party\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.

In no event shall either party be liable to the other party for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages arising out of or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, regardless of whether such damages are based on contract, tort, strict liability, or any other theory, and regardless of whether such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages; provided, however, that this sentence shall not limit the liability of a party with respect to third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under the Transition Services Agreement.

The parties acknowledge and agree that the foregoing limitations on liability reflect the parties\' agreement regarding the allocation of risk under the Transition Services Agreement, and that neither party would have entered into this Agreement without such limitations.

**Section 7.12(e) --- Cooperation**

During the Transition Period, Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish its own capability to perform the Transition Services independently and to reduce its reliance on Seller for the provision of such Transition Services as promptly as reasonably practicable. Buyer shall dedicate appropriate internal resources, including qualified personnel and financial resources, to the transition effort and shall develop and implement a transition plan in consultation with Seller.

Seller shall cooperate in good faith with Buyer\'s efforts to transition the Transition Services to Buyer\'s own systems, personnel, and third-party providers. Such cooperation shall include reasonable knowledge transfer, documentation of processes and procedures, and making Seller\'s personnel reasonably available for consultations during normal business hours.

Nothing in this Section 7.12 or the Transition Services Agreement shall require Seller to:

> \(i\) maintain any employee in employment or any contractor engagement solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services;
>
> \(ii\) acquire, license, or maintain any hardware, software, or other technology solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services, except to the extent that Seller was licensing or maintaining such technology for the benefit of the Business as of the Closing Date and the cost of such license or maintenance is included in the Fully-Loaded Cost;
