\"**Transferred Employees**\" means those approximately one thousand one hundred eighty (1,180) employees of the Business who will transfer to Trident at the Closing in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Purchase Agreement.
**[ARTICLE 2 --- SERVICES]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1** *Provision of Services.* Commencing on the Effective Date and continuing during the Term, Service Provider shall provide, or shall cause its Affiliates or designees to provide, to Service Recipient the Services described in the following Schedules:
> \(a\) **Schedule A** --- Financial Reporting & Accounting Services;
> \(b\) **Schedule B** --- Information Technology Services;
> \(c\) **Schedule C** --- Human Resources Services;
> \(d\) **Schedule D** --- Supply Chain & Procurement Services;
> \(e\) **Schedule E** --- Regulatory & EHS Compliance Services; and
> \(f\) **Schedule F** --- Treasury & Tax Services.

The six (6) service categories set forth above correspond to the service categories identified in Exhibit H to the Purchase Agreement. The Services will be provided by an aggregate of approximately one hundred (100) full-time equivalent Service Provider personnel allocated across the service categories as follows: twenty-two (22) FTEs for Financial Reporting & Accounting; thirty-one (31) FTEs for Information Technology; eighteen (18) FTEs for Human Resources; fourteen (14) FTEs for Supply Chain & Procurement; eight (8) FTEs for Regulatory & EHS Compliance; and seven (7) FTEs for Treasury & Tax. The specific scope, deliverables, personnel, systems, and migration milestones for each Service category are set forth in the applicable Schedule. In the event of any conflict between the terms of an individual Schedule and the terms of this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Schedule expressly and specifically provides otherwise.

**Section 2.2** *Scope Limitations.* The Services to be provided by Service Provider under this Agreement are limited solely and exclusively to those services expressly described in Schedules A through F. Service Provider shall not be obligated to provide any service or perform any function that is not expressly described in the applicable Schedule. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Service Provider shall not be obligated to: (a) hire additional employees or engage additional contractors solely for the purpose of providing the Services; (b) acquire, lease, or license additional equipment, software, or other assets solely for the purpose of providing the Services; (c) maintain any third-party software license, service contract, or other agreement beyond its current term or renewal period solely for the purpose of providing the Services; or (d) make any capital expenditure solely for the purpose of providing the Services. The scope of each Service is as described in the applicable Schedule as of the Effective Date, and no expansion, modification, or enhancement of any Service shall be required of Service Provider except as may be mutually agreed in writing by the Parties.

**Section 2.3** *Exclusive Remedy.* Service Recipient\'s sole and exclusive remedy for any failure by Service Provider to perform any of the Services in accordance with this Agreement shall be as expressly set forth in Article 9 (Indemnification) and Article 10 (Limitation of Liability). Service Recipient shall have no other right or remedy at law or in equity with respect to any such failure, except as expressly set forth herein.

**Section 2.4** *Subcontracting.* Service Provider may, in its sole discretion, subcontract or delegate any or all of the Services to qualified third-party subcontractors or to Affiliates of Service Provider; provided that Service Provider shall remain fully responsible for the performance of any subcontracted or delegated Services and for the acts and omissions of any such subcontractor or Affiliate to the same extent as if Service Provider had performed such Services directly. Service Provider shall ensure that any subcontractor or Affiliate performing Services is bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in Article 8.
**[ARTICLE 3 --- SERVICE STANDARDS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1** *Standard of Performance.* Service Provider shall perform, or cause to be performed, each of the Services at a level of quality, timeliness, and competence at least equal to or better than the level at which such services were provided to the Business during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to the Closing Date, and in all cases in accordance with industry best practices applicable to each such Service (the \"**Service Standard**\"). Service Provider shall allocate sufficient resources, including qualified personnel and appropriate systems, to meet the Service Standard at all times during the Term. In the event of any dispute regarding the Service Standard, the Parties shall refer the matter to the Steering Committee for resolution in accordance with Article 4.

**Section 3.2** *No Guarantee of Results.* Notwithstanding Section 3.1 or any other provision of this Agreement, Service Provider does not guarantee any particular outcome, result, or deliverable from the provision of the Services. Service Provider\'s obligation is limited to performing the Services in accordance with the Service Standard, and Service Provider shall not be liable for any failure to achieve a particular business outcome or result so long as the Services are performed in accordance with the Service Standard.

**Section 3.3** *Cooperation.* Service Recipient shall cooperate with Service Provider and shall provide, in a timely manner, all information, data, access, approvals, decisions, and assistance reasonably necessary for Service Provider to perform the Services in accordance with this Agreement. Service Recipient acknowledges and agrees that Service Provider\'s ability to meet the Service Standard may be materially and adversely affected by Service Recipient\'s failure to cooperate or to provide timely information, access, or decisions as contemplated by this Section 3.3. Service Provider shall not be liable for any failure or delay in performing the Services to the extent such failure or delay is attributable to Service Recipient\'s failure to comply with this Section 3.3.
**[ARTICLE 4 --- GOVERNANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1** *Steering Committee.* Within ten (10) Business Days of the Effective Date, each Party shall designate two (2) senior representatives to serve on a joint transition steering committee (the \"**Steering Committee**\"). The initial designees of the Steering Committee shall be as follows:
> \(a\) **For Service Provider (Polaris):**
> \(i\) David K. Okafor, Chief Financial Officer; and
> \(ii\) Sharon M. Petrosian, General Counsel.
> \(b\) **For Service Recipient (Trident):**
> \(i\) Patricia N. Suresh, Chief Financial Officer; and
> \(ii\) Robert F. Collier, General Counsel.

Either Party may replace its designees on the Steering Committee at any time upon written notice to the other Party; provided that any replacement designee shall be a senior officer of the designating Party with sufficient authority to make decisions on behalf of such Party with respect to matters arising under this Agreement. The Steering Committee shall meet at least once per calendar month (or more frequently as mutually agreed or as circumstances require) to review and discuss the status of service delivery, migration milestones, key performance metrics, open issues, and any disputes or concerns raised by either Party. Meetings may be held in person or by video or telephone conference. Each Party shall bear its own costs associated with participation in the Steering Committee. The Steering Committee shall not have the authority to amend, modify, or waive any provision of this Agreement, which may be done only in accordance with Section 15.6.

**Section 4.2** *Service Managers.* In addition to its Steering Committee designees, each Party shall designate a Service Manager for each Service category (each, a \"**Service Manager**\") who shall serve as the primary point of contact for day-to-day operational matters relating to such Service category. Each Service Manager shall be an individual with relevant operational expertise and sufficient authority to manage day-to-day decisions within the scope of the applicable Service category. Service Managers shall report regularly to the Steering Committee and shall escalate to the Steering Committee any issues that cannot be resolved at the operational level within a reasonable period of time. Each Party shall notify the other Party in writing of the identity and contact information of its Service Managers within five (5) Business Days of the Effective Date.

**Section 4.3** *Key Personnel.* Service Provider shall ensure that the individuals identified on Schedule H attached hereto (the \"**Key Personnel**\") are assigned to perform the Services during the Term at the FTE allocation levels set forth on Schedule H. Service Provider shall not reassign, transfer, terminate (other than for cause as determined by Service Provider in its reasonable judgment), or otherwise remove any Key Personnel from the performance of the Services without the prior written consent of Service Recipient, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. In the event that any Key Personnel individual voluntarily resigns, becomes permanently disabled, or is terminated for cause, Service Provider shall promptly notify Service Recipient and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to replace such individual with a person of substantially similar qualifications, experience, and skill within thirty (30) days, subject to Service Recipient\'s prior written approval of the replacement (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed). Service Provider acknowledges that the Key Personnel possess specialized knowledge of the Business and that their continued involvement is material to the successful transition of the Business to Service Recipient.

**Section 4.4** *Reporting.* Service Provider shall deliver to Service Recipient, within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, a written report summarizing the Services performed during such month (each, a \"**Monthly Report**\"). Each Monthly Report shall include, at a minimum: (a) hours worked by each FTE assigned to the Services, broken down by Service category; (b) a summary of any material issues, disruptions, or failures in service delivery; (c) a status update on migration milestones, including any variances from the milestone schedule set forth in the applicable Schedule; and (d) such other information as the Steering Committee may reasonably request from time to time.
**[ARTICLE 5 --- TERM AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1** *Initial Term.* This Agreement shall become effective on the Closing Date and shall continue for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Initial Term**\"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article 5. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement shall have no force or effect unless and until the Closing occurs under the Purchase Agreement.

**Section 5.2** *Automatic Renewal.* Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive six (6)-month periods (each, a \"**Renewal Term**\"), unless Service Provider delivers written notice of non-renewal to Service Recipient at least one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term, as applicable. The Agreement may be renewed for up to two (2) successive Renewal Terms pursuant to this Section 5.2. During any Renewal Term, all terms and conditions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, including the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule, subject to any adjustments expressly provided for herein. For the avoidance of doubt, the burden of providing notice of non-renewal rests solely with Service Provider; failure by Service Provider to deliver timely notice of non-renewal shall result in automatic renewal for the next succeeding Renewal Term (subject to the two (2) Renewal Term maximum).

**Section 5.3** *Termination of Individual Services.* Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, provided that such notice specifies in reasonable detail the Service to be terminated and the effective date of termination. Termination of an individual Service shall not affect the continuance of any other Service being provided under this Agreement. Upon termination of any individual Service, the corresponding Fees for such Service shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of such termination.

**Section 5.4** *Termination for Cause.* Either Party may terminate this Agreement in whole, or with respect to any individual Service, upon written notice to the other Party if the other Party materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice from the non-breaching Party specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail. If the breach is of such a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, the breaching Party shall not be deemed in default so long as it commences cure within such thirty (30)-day period and thereafter diligently prosecutes such cure to completion; provided, however, that no cure period shall extend beyond ninety (90) days from the date of the initial notice of breach.
**Section 5.5** *Effect of Termination.* Upon termination or expiration of any Service or of this Agreement (in whole or in part):
> \(a\) Service Provider\'s obligation to provide the terminated or expired Services shall immediately cease as of the effective date of such termination or expiration;

> \(b\) Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider all accrued but unpaid Fees and expenses for Services actually performed through the effective date of termination or expiration, which payment shall be made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration;

> \(c\) each Party shall promptly return to the other Party, or at the other Party\'s election destroy and certify in writing the destruction of, all Confidential Information of the other Party that relates to the terminated or expired Services, except to the extent that retention is required by Applicable Law or bona fide document retention policies (in which case such retained Confidential Information shall remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of Article 8); and
> \(d\) all rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the terminated or expired Services shall cease, except as expressly provided in Section 5.6 (Survival).

**Section 5.6** *Survival.* The provisions of Article 1 (Definitions), Article 7 (Intellectual Property), Article 8 (Confidentiality), Article 9 (Indemnification), Article 10 (Limitation of Liability), Article 11 (Representations and Warranties), Article 13 (Insurance), Article 14 (Audit Rights), and Article 15 (General Provisions) shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement in accordance with their respective terms.
**[ARTICLE 6 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1** *Service Charges.* In consideration for the provision of the Services, Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule (Schedule G) for each Service during the Term. The Fees for each Service category are calculated on a cost-plus basis reflecting Service Provider\'s fully-loaded cost of providing the applicable Service (including personnel costs, allocated overhead, and systems costs), plus a markup as set forth on the Fee Schedule. The Fees represent the sole compensation to which Service Provider is entitled for the provision of the Services, and Service Provider shall not charge Service Recipient for any internal costs, overhead, or administrative expenses except as expressly reflected in the Fee Schedule.

**Section 6.2** *Invoicing.* Service Provider shall deliver to Service Recipient a monthly invoice within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, setting forth in reasonable detail the Services performed during such month, the applicable FTE hours, and the Fees due for such month. Each invoice shall be accompanied by such supporting documentation as Service Recipient may reasonably request to verify the accuracy of the amounts invoiced. Invoices shall be delivered to the attention of Service Recipient\'s Service Manager for the applicable Service category, with a copy to Service Recipient\'s Chief Financial Officer.

**Section 6.3** *Payment.* Service Recipient shall pay each undisputed invoice within a commercially reasonable time following receipt thereof. All payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Service Provider in writing from time to time.

**Section 6.4** *Fee Escalation.* The Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule are fixed for the duration of the Term and shall not be subject to escalation or adjustment, except as expressly provided in this Agreement.

**Section 6.5** *Taxes.* All Fees stated in this Agreement and on the Fee Schedule are exclusive of any applicable sales, use, value-added, goods and services, or similar Taxes (collectively, \"**Transaction Taxes**\"). Service Recipient shall be responsible for and shall pay, or reimburse Service Provider for, all Transaction Taxes imposed on or with respect to the Services, other than Taxes measured by Service Provider\'s net income, capital, or franchise. Service Provider shall separately state any Transaction Taxes on its invoices. Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize Transaction Taxes and shall cooperate in good faith with the other Party to obtain any available exemptions or reduced rates for such Taxes.

**Section 6.6** *Disputed Amounts.* If Service Recipient disputes any amount set forth on an invoice in good faith, Service Recipient shall: (a) pay the undisputed portion of such invoice when due in accordance with Section 6.3; (b) provide written notice to Service Provider of the disputed amount, specifying in reasonable detail the basis for the dispute, within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the applicable invoice; and (c) work in good faith with Service Provider to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days after such notice. If the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within such thirty (30)-day period, either Party may escalate the matter to the Steering Committee. Pending resolution of any disputed amount, Service Provider shall continue to perform the Services without interruption.
**[ARTICLE 7 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1** *Service Provider Materials --- License Grant.* Service Provider hereby grants to Service Recipient a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, and create derivative works of any Service Provider Materials (including any tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, or know-how) developed or utilized by Service Provider in connection with the performance of the Services under this Agreement. This license shall include the right to sublicense to Service Recipient\'s Affiliates, successors, and assigns, and shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason. For the avoidance of doubt, the foregoing license extends to all Service Provider Materials that are used, in whole or in part, in the delivery of any of the Services, regardless of whether such Service Provider Materials were created specifically for the Services or existed prior to the Effective Date and were adapted or applied in the course of service delivery. Nothing in this Section 7.1 shall be construed to transfer ownership of any Service Provider Materials to Service Recipient; Service Provider retains all right, title, and interest in and to the Service Provider Materials, subject to the license granted herein.

**Section 7.2** *Service Recipient Materials.* Service Recipient retains all right, title, and interest in and to any data, materials, information, documents, or other content provided by Service Recipient to Service Provider for purposes of the Services (collectively, \"**Service Recipient Materials**\"). Service Provider shall use the Service Recipient Materials solely for the purpose of performing the Services under this Agreement and for no other purpose. Upon termination or expiration of any Service or this Agreement, Service Provider shall promptly return or, at Service Recipient\'s election, destroy all Service Recipient Materials in its possession or control.

**Section 7.3** *Feedback.* To the extent that Service Recipient provides any suggestions, ideas, enhancement requests, recommendations, or other feedback to Service Provider regarding the Service Provider Materials or any other intellectual property of Service Provider (collectively, \"**Feedback**\"), Service Recipient hereby assigns to Service Provider all right, title, and interest in and to such Feedback and agrees that Service Provider is free to use, disclose, reproduce, license, and otherwise distribute and exploit such Feedback as it sees fit, without obligation or restriction of any kind. Service Recipient acknowledges that this assignment is irrevocable and that no additional consideration is required.
**[ARTICLE 8 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1** *Confidentiality Obligations.* Each Party agrees to hold the other Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence and to protect such Confidential Information using the same degree of care that it uses to protect its own confidential information of like kind, but in no event less than a reasonable degree of care. Neither Party shall disclose the other Party\'s Confidential Information to any Person, except to its Representatives who have a bona fide need to know such information for the purpose of performing obligations or exercising rights under this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 8. Each Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 8 by its Representatives. Neither Party shall use the other Party\'s Confidential Information for any purpose other than in connection with the performance of its obligations or the exercise of its rights under this Agreement. Without limiting the foregoing, neither Party shall reverse engineer, decompile, or disassemble any Confidential Information of the other Party.
**Section 8.2** *Exceptions.* The obligations set forth in Section 8.1 shall not apply to any information that:
> \(a\) is or becomes publicly available other than as a result of a disclosure by the Receiving Party or its Representatives in breach of this Agreement;
> \(b\) was already known to the Receiving Party at the time of disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by competent written records of the Receiving Party;

> \(c\) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by competent written records of the Receiving Party; or
> \(d\) is received by the Receiving Party from a third party who is not, to the Receiving Party\'s knowledge, bound by any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information.

In addition, the Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by Applicable Law, regulation, or order of a Governmental Authority, or by the rules and regulations of a stock exchange on which the Receiving Party\'s (or its parent\'s) securities are listed; provided that the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide prompt written notice to the Disclosing Party of such required disclosure so as to enable the Disclosing Party to seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy. If a protective order or other remedy is not obtained, the Receiving Party shall disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information that it is legally required to disclose and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain reliable assurance that confidential treatment will be given to such disclosed information.

**Section 8.3** *Survival of Confidentiality.* The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 8 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years following the effective date of such expiration or termination.

**Section 8.4** *Data Privacy.* Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws of the United States in connection with its performance under this Agreement, including with respect to the collection, use, processing, storage, transfer, and disposal of any personally identifiable information of employees, customers, or other individuals. Each Party shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.
**[ARTICLE 9 --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1** *Service Recipient Indemnification.* Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (each, a \"**Service Provider Indemnitee**\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or suffered by any Service Provider Indemnitee arising out of or relating to:
> \(a\) Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance on the Services or the results thereof;
> \(b\) any breach by Service Recipient of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation under this Agreement;
> \(c\) any negligent or wrongful act or omission of Service Recipient or its employees, agents, or contractors in connection with this Agreement; or

> \(d\) any claim by a third party arising out of Service Recipient\'s use of the Services or any deliverables provided hereunder, except to the extent such claim arises from Service Provider\'s gross negligence or willful misconduct.

**Section 9.2** *Service Provider Indemnification.* Service Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Recipient and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (each, a \"**Service Recipient Indemnitee**\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or suffered by any Service Recipient Indemnitee arising out of or relating to:
> \(a\) any gross negligence or willful misconduct of Service Provider, its Affiliates, or their respective employees, agents, or contractors in performing the Services;
> \(b\) any breach by Service Provider of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation under this Agreement; or
> \(c\) any violation of Applicable Law by Service Provider, its Affiliates, or their respective employees, agents, or contractors in performing the Services.
**Section 9.3** *Indemnification Procedures.* The following procedures shall apply to any claim for indemnification under this Article 9:

> \(a\) **Notice.** The Party seeking indemnification (the \"**Indemnified Party**\") shall promptly notify the other Party (the \"**Indemnifying Party**\") in writing of any claim, demand, suit, action, or proceeding for which indemnification is sought (a \"**Claim**\"), specifying in reasonable detail the nature of the Claim and the amount of Losses incurred or expected to be incurred (to the extent then known). The failure by the Indemnified Party to give timely notice shall not relieve the Indemnifying Party of its indemnification obligations except to the extent that the Indemnifying Party is actually and materially prejudiced by such failure.

> \(b\) **Defense of Third-Party Claims.** Upon receipt of notice of a Claim involving a third-party claim, the Indemnifying Party shall have the right, but not the obligation, to assume the defense of such third-party claim, including the employment of counsel reasonably satisfactory to the Indemnified Party, at the Indemnifying Party\'s sole cost and expense. If the Indemnifying Party assumes the defense, the Indemnified Party may participate in the defense at its own expense, but the Indemnifying Party shall control all aspects of the defense and any related settlement or compromise. If the Indemnifying Party does not assume the defense within thirty (30) days after receipt of notice, the Indemnified Party may defend the third-party claim at the Indemnifying Party\'s expense.

> \(c\) **Settlement.** The Indemnifying Party shall not consent to entry of any judgment or enter into any settlement or compromise with respect to a third-party claim without the prior written consent of the Indemnified Party (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), unless such judgment, settlement, or compromise: (i) includes an unconditional release of the Indemnified Party from all liability with respect to such claim; (ii) does not impose any non-monetary obligations on the Indemnified Party; and (iii) does not contain any admission of liability or wrongdoing by the Indemnified Party.

> \(d\) **Cooperation.** The Indemnified Party shall cooperate in all reasonable respects with the Indemnifying Party and its counsel in the defense of any third-party claim, including by making available relevant records, information, and personnel.
**[ARTICLE 10 --- LIMITATION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1** *Aggregate Liability Cap.* Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Service Provider\'s aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or any other legal or equitable theory, shall not exceed an amount equal to two hundred percent (200%) of the total Service Charges actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider under this Agreement as of the date of the applicable claim (the \"**Liability Cap**\"). For the avoidance of doubt, the Liability Cap shall apply to all claims in the aggregate and not on a per-claim basis. This Section 10.1 shall not limit Service Provider\'s liability for fraud, willful misconduct, or breaches of Article 8 (Confidentiality).

**Section 10.2** *Consequential Damages.* SERVICE PROVIDER HEREBY WAIVES, AND SHALL NOT ASSERT, ANY AND ALL CLAIMS AGAINST SERVICE RECIPIENT FOR CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, EXEMPLARY, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, COST OF REPLACEMENT SERVICES, DIMINUTION OF VALUE, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SUCH DAMAGES ARE BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, AND REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SERVICE PROVIDER HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. THE FOREGOING WAIVER SHALL APPLY EVEN IN THE EVENT OF THE FAILURE OF ESSENTIAL PURPOSE OF ANY REMEDY.

**Section 10.3** *Essential Basis.* The Parties acknowledge and agree that the limitations and exclusions of liability set forth in this Article 10 represent a fundamental element of the basis of the bargain between the Parties and that the Parties would not have entered into this Agreement absent such limitations and exclusions. Such limitations and exclusions shall apply regardless of the failure of essential purpose of any remedy provided herein and shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement.
**[ARTICLE 11 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**
**Section 11.1** *Mutual Representations.* Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party as of the Effective Date that:
> \(a\) it is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its incorporation;
> \(b\) it has the full corporate power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby;
> \(c\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by such Party have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action on the part of such Party;

> \(d\) this Agreement constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and

> \(e\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by such Party do not and will not violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party\'s organizational documents, any Applicable Law, or any material agreement to which such Party is a party or by which such Party\'s assets are bound.
**Section 11.2** *Service Provider Representations.* Service Provider further represents and warrants to Service Recipient as of the Effective Date that:
> \(a\) Service Provider has the personnel, systems, facilities, and capabilities necessary and sufficient to perform the Services as of the Effective Date;
> \(b\) the Services will be performed in compliance with all Applicable Laws and regulations; and
> \(c\) Service Provider has not received any written notice from any Governmental Authority that would reasonably be expected to materially impair its ability to perform the Services.

**Section 11.3** *Disclaimer.* EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, SERVICE PROVIDER MAKES NO REPRESENTATIONS OR WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, STATUTORY OR OTHERWISE, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, TITLE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, OR QUALITY, AND ALL SUCH WARRANTIES ARE HEREBY EXPRESSLY DISCLAIMED. SERVICE RECIPIENT ACKNOWLEDGES THAT IT IS NOT RELYING ON ANY REPRESENTATIONS OR WARRANTIES NOT EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT.
**[ARTICLE 12 --- FORCE MAJEURE]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1** *Force Majeure.* Neither Party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Agreement to the extent such failure or delay results from a Force Majeure Event. The affected Party shall: (a) promptly notify the other Party in writing of the Force Majeure Event, describing in reasonable detail the nature of the event and the expected duration thereof; (b) use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance of its obligations as soon as practicable; and (c) keep the other Party reasonably informed of the status of such Force Majeure Event and its efforts to resume performance. The non-affected Party shall cooperate in good faith with the affected Party\'s mitigation efforts. A Force Majeure Event shall not excuse the affected Party\'s obligation to make any payment that was due and owing prior to the occurrence of such Force Majeure Event.

**Section 12.2** *Allocation During Force Majeure.* During any period in which performance of any Service is affected by a Force Majeure Event, the Fees for the affected Service shall be equitably adjusted to reflect the actual level of Services delivered during such period. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to agree upon an appropriate adjustment. If the Parties are unable to agree upon an appropriate adjustment within fifteen (15) Business Days, either Party may refer the matter to the Steering Committee for resolution.
**[ARTICLE 13 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 13.1** *Service Recipient Insurance.* Service Recipient shall maintain, at its own expense, during the Term and for a period of twelve (12) months following the expiration or termination of this Agreement, commercial general liability insurance with a per-occurrence limit of not less than Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) and an annual aggregate limit of not less than Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000), issued by an insurer rated not less than \"A-\" (Excellent) by A.M. Best Company. Such insurance shall provide coverage for bodily injury, property damage, personal injury, and advertising injury arising out of or relating to Service Recipient\'s operations and performance under this Agreement.

**Section 13.2** *Service Provider Insurance.* Service Provider shall maintain, at its own expense, during the Term and for a period of twelve (12) months following the expiration or termination of this Agreement, the following insurance coverages:

> \(a\) commercial general liability insurance with a per-occurrence limit of not less than Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) and an annual aggregate limit of not less than Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000);
> \(b\) workers\' compensation insurance as required by Applicable Law in each jurisdiction in which Service Provider\'s employees perform Services; and

> \(c\) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance with a per-occurrence limit of not less than Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) and an annual aggregate limit of not less than Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000).

All insurance required under this Section 13.2 shall be issued by insurers rated not less than \"A-\" (Excellent) by A.M. Best Company. Service Provider shall provide Service Recipient with certificates of insurance evidencing the foregoing coverages upon request.
**[ARTICLE 14 --- AUDIT RIGHTS]{.underline}**

**Section 14.1** *Audit Rights.* Service Recipient shall have the right, at Service Provider\'s expense, to audit the books, records, systems, and supporting documentation of Service Provider relating to the Service Charges and the performance of the Services up to two (2) times per calendar year. Service Recipient shall provide Service Provider with at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice of any such audit, specifying the scope and expected duration of the audit. Audits shall be conducted during normal business hours at Service Provider\'s principal offices or such other location where the applicable records are maintained and shall not unreasonably interfere with Service Provider\'s business operations. Service Recipient may conduct such audits using its internal audit personnel or an independent third-party auditor selected by Service Recipient (at Service Provider\'s expense); provided that any third-party auditor shall be bound by confidentiality obligations reasonably satisfactory to Service Provider. Service Provider shall cooperate fully with any audit conducted under this Section 14.1 and shall provide reasonable access to its personnel, books, records, systems, and facilities.

**Section 14.2** *Audit Adjustments.* If an audit conducted pursuant to Section 14.1 reveals that Service Provider has overcharged Service Recipient for any Service, Service Provider shall credit the amount of such overpayment to Service Recipient within thirty (30) days following Service Recipient\'s written demand, together with interest on such amount at a rate of the lesser of one percent (1%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, calculated from the date of the overpayment through the date of the credit. If an audit reveals that Service Provider has undercharged Service Recipient for any Service, Service Recipient shall pay the amount of such deficiency to Service Provider within thirty (30) days following Service Provider\'s written demand.
**[ARTICLE 15 --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 15.1** *Governing Law.* This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio, without regard to its conflict of laws principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**Section 15.2** *Dispute Resolution.* Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination, shall be resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Cuyahoga County, Ohio. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts for the purpose of any such dispute, controversy, or claim and irrevocably waives, and agrees not to assert by way of motion, defense, or otherwise, any objection to such jurisdiction or venue, including any objection based on the doctrine of inconvenient forum or any objection to the laying of venue in Cuyahoga County, Ohio. EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ALL RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION, PROCEEDING, OR COUNTERCLAIM ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

**Section 15.3** *Notices.* All notices, requests, demands, consents, waivers, and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given: (a) when delivered by hand or by a nationally recognized overnight courier service (receipt requested); (b) on the date sent by email (with confirmation of transmission), provided that a copy is also sent by overnight courier service on the same day; or (c) on the third (3rd) Business Day after deposit in the U.S. mail, by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid. All notices shall be addressed as follows:

> Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. 1200 Commonwealth Avenue, Suite 3000 Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 15222

Service Recipient shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish its own general ledger, financial reporting, and accounting systems within twelve (12) months of the Closing Date. Service Provider shall provide reasonable cooperation and data extraction support to facilitate the migration, including provision of historical financial data in machine-readable format. The target cutover from Service Provider\'s systems to Service Recipient\'s systems shall occur no later than the expiration of the Initial Term. The Parties shall develop a detailed migration plan within sixty (60) days of the Effective Date.

The Fees and scope of Services set forth in this Schedule A are based upon the following assumptions and dependencies: (a) Service Recipient will provide timely data, approvals, authorizations, and access to Transferred Employees for queries and issue resolution; (b) transaction volumes will remain consistent with historical levels (plus or minus 10%); (c) Service Provider will have continued access to the Business\'s historical financial data for lookback purposes; and (d) no material changes to the chart of accounts structure are required during the Service Period.
**SCHEDULE B** **INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SERVICES**
**1. Service Description**
Service Provider shall provide the following information technology services to Service Recipient during the applicable Service Period:

> \(a\) **ERP System Access and Support.** Continued access to and support of Service Provider\'s SAP S/4HANA enterprise resource planning system for the Business, including the following modules: Finance (FI/CO), Materials Management (MM), Sales and Distribution (SD), Production Planning (PP), Quality Management (QM), and Plant Maintenance (PM). Service Provider shall maintain the system in operational condition, apply necessary patches and updates in accordance with its standard maintenance schedule, and provide Tier 2 and Tier 3 SAP application support for Business users.

> \(b\) **Network Infrastructure Support.** Management and maintenance of the wide area network (WAN), local area network (LAN), and virtual private network (VPN) infrastructure supporting the Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; Greenville, South Carolina; and Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico facilities, to the extent such infrastructure is shared with or provided by Service Provider. This includes router and switch management, bandwidth monitoring, and connectivity to Service Provider\'s data center.

> \(c\) **Cybersecurity Monitoring and Incident Response.** Monitoring of the Business\'s IT environment for cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, and incidents using Service Provider\'s existing security information and event management (SIEM) platform, endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools, and intrusion detection systems. In the event of a cybersecurity incident that affects or reasonably could be expected to affect Business data, Service Provider shall notify Service Recipient within seventy-two (72) hours of Service Provider\'s becoming aware of such incident and shall cooperate with Service Recipient in investigating and remediating the incident.

> \(d\) **IT Help Desk Support.** Tier 1 and Tier 2 IT help desk support for Business users, available during normal business hours (8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. local time at each facility, Monday through Friday, excluding holidays). Service Provider shall maintain a ticketing system for tracking and resolving help desk requests and shall provide monthly summary reports on ticket volume, resolution times, and open issues.

> \(e\) **Email and Collaboration Tools.** Continued access to Service Provider\'s Microsoft 365 environment, including Exchange Online (email), SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, and Microsoft Teams, for Business users. Service Provider shall maintain user accounts, distribution lists, and shared mailboxes for the Business during the Service Period.

> \(f\) **Data Backup and Disaster Recovery.** Data backup services for Business data stored on Service Provider\'s systems, including daily incremental backups and weekly full backups. Service Provider shall maintain disaster recovery capabilities consistent with its existing disaster recovery plan and shall include the Business\'s critical systems and data in such plan during the Service Period.
**2. Service Provider Personnel**
Service Provider shall assign approximately thirty-one (31) full-time equivalent personnel to provide the Information Technology Services, including the following roles:
**Role**                            **FTE Count**
IT Director                         1
Senior Systems Administrators       4
SAP Basis Administrators            3
Network Engineers                   5
Cybersecurity Analysts              3
Help Desk Technicians               8
Database Administrators             2

IT Project Managers                 2
**3. Systems and Tools**

The following systems and tools shall be used in the delivery of the Information Technology Services: SAP S/4HANA (all applicable modules), Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, Teams), Service Provider\'s network infrastructure (WAN/LAN/VPN), Service Provider\'s cybersecurity platform (SIEM, EDR, IDS), and Service Provider\'s backup and disaster recovery systems.
**4. Service Period**
From the Effective Date through the earlier of: (a) termination of this Service in accordance with Article 5; or (b) expiration of the Term.
**5. Fees**
**Base Monthly Cost:**              **\$340,000**
Markup:                             15%
Monthly Fee:                        \$391,000
**6. Migration Milestones**

Service Recipient shall use commercially reasonable efforts to implement its own enterprise resource planning system and complete the migration of all Business data from Service Provider\'s systems to Service Recipient\'s systems within eighteen (18) months of the Closing Date. Service Provider shall provide reasonable cooperation with data extraction, data mapping, and migration testing activities. The Parties shall develop a detailed IT migration plan, including data extraction schedules, testing protocols, and cutover criteria, within ninety (90) days of the Effective Date.
**7. Data Segregation**

Service Provider shall implement logical access controls separating Business data from other Polaris divisional data within Service Provider\'s SAP S/4HANA system and other shared IT systems within thirty (30) days of the Closing Date. Such logical access controls shall ensure that Service Recipient\'s authorized users can access only Business data, and that Service Provider\'s personnel who are not involved in providing the Services cannot access Business data without authorization. Service Provider shall provide Service Recipient with a written description of the implemented access controls within forty-five (45) days of the Closing Date.
**8. Cybersecurity Incident Response**

In the event of a security incident affecting Business data, Service Provider shall: (a) notify Service Recipient within seventy-two (72) hours of becoming aware of the incident; (b) take commercially reasonable steps to contain and mitigate the incident; (c) cooperate with Service Recipient in investigating the root cause and scope of the incident; and (d) provide a written post-incident report to Service Recipient within thirty (30) days of resolution. Service Provider shall maintain cybersecurity monitoring consistent with its existing protocols and industry-standard practices throughout the Service Period.
**SCHEDULE C** **HUMAN RESOURCES SERVICES**
**1. Service Description**
Service Provider shall provide the following human resources services to Service Recipient during the applicable Service Period:

> \(a\) **Payroll Processing.** Processing of payroll for approximately one thousand one hundred eighty (1,180) Transferred Employees located at the Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; Greenville, South Carolina; and Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico facilities, including calculation of gross and net pay, Tax withholding and remittance (federal, state, and local in the United States; applicable payroll taxes in Mexico), direct deposit processing, payroll check issuance (as needed), and preparation and filing of all required payroll Tax returns and reports (including Forms W-2, 941, and state equivalents in the United States, and the corresponding filings required under Mexican law). Payroll shall be processed on Service Provider\'s existing payroll cycle (bi-weekly for U.S. employees; bi-monthly for Mexico employees).

> \(b\) **Benefits Administration.** Administration of employee benefits programs for Transferred Employees during the transition period, including medical, dental, and vision insurance plans; 401(k) retirement savings plan (U.S. employees); life insurance and disability coverage; flexible spending accounts; and employee assistance program. Service Provider shall continue to administer the existing benefit plans in which Transferred Employees participated immediately prior to the Closing until Service Recipient establishes its own benefits programs and enrolls Transferred Employees therein.

> \(c\) **HRIS System Access.** Continued access to Service Provider\'s HRIS/SAP HCM module for purposes of maintaining employee records for Transferred Employees, including personal information, employment history, compensation data, benefits enrollment, performance records, and leave balances.

> \(d\) **Workers\' Compensation Claims Management.** Management of legacy workers\' compensation claims for Transferred Employees that arose prior to or during the transition period, including claims administration, communication with claims adjusters and medical providers, and coordination with Service Recipient\'s safety personnel.

> \(e\) **New Hire Onboarding Support.** Assistance with onboarding of Service Recipient\'s replacement hires for positions previously filled by Service Provider shared-services personnel, including provision of access to onboarding templates, policy documents, and standard operating procedures.

> \(f\) **Employee Records Management.** Maintenance and secure storage of employee records for Transferred Employees during the Service Period, with transfer of records to Service Recipient upon termination of this Service. All records shall be maintained in compliance with applicable law, including retention requirements.
**2. Service Provider Personnel**
Service Provider shall assign approximately eighteen (18) full-time equivalent personnel to provide the Human Resources Services, including the following roles:

From the Effective Date through the earlier of: (a) termination of this Service in accordance with Article 5; or (b) expiration of the Term.

Service Provider shall process Mexican payroll on a bi-monthly basis and shall prepare and file all required employer contributions and filings with the relevant Mexican governmental authorities.

Service Provider shall cooperate with Service Recipient in the transition of employee records and payroll data and shall provide historical payroll data in machine-readable format upon request.

**SCHEDULE D** **SUPPLY CHAIN & PROCUREMENT SERVICES**
**1. Service Description**
Service Provider shall provide the following supply chain and procurement services to Service Recipient during the applicable Service Period:

> \(a\) **Raw Material Sourcing.** Coordination of raw material sourcing for the Business under Service Provider\'s existing master supply agreements, covering the following key raw material categories: titanium dioxide (TiO2); epoxy resins; polyurethane intermediates; and specialty solvents. Service Provider shall place purchase orders, manage order confirmations, and coordinate delivery schedules for raw materials required by the Business in accordance with Service Recipient\'s procurement requests and production schedules.

> \(b\) **Logistics Coordination.** Coordination of inbound logistics for raw materials delivered to the Pittsburgh, Greenville, and Monterrey facilities, and outbound logistics for finished goods shipped from such facilities, utilizing Service Provider\'s existing logistics management platform and relationships with third-party freight carriers and logistics providers.

> \(c\) **Warehouse Management.** Management of warehousing operations at the Pittsburgh shared facility (Building 7), which is shared with Service Provider\'s Advanced Materials Division. This includes receiving, storage, inventory tracking, picking, packing, and shipping for the Business\'s raw materials and finished goods inventory allocated to Building 7.

> \(d\) **Purchase Order Processing.** Processing of purchase requisitions and purchase orders through Service Provider\'s SAP S/4HANA Materials Management (MM) module on behalf of the Business, including requisition approval workflows, purchase order generation, goods receipt processing, and invoice verification.

> \(e\) **Vendor Management and Relationship Transition Support.** Assistance with transitioning vendor relationships from Service Provider to Service Recipient, including introductions to key vendors, provision of historical purchasing data and pricing information, and support for Service Recipient\'s efforts to negotiate and establish its own supply agreements.

**SCHEDULE E** **REGULATORY & EHS COMPLIANCE SERVICES**
**1. Service Description**
Service Provider shall provide the following regulatory and environmental, health, and safety (EHS) compliance services to Service Recipient during the applicable Service Period:

> \(a\) **Environmental Permit Maintenance and Renewal.** Maintenance and renewal of environmental permits for the Greenville, South Carolina facility, including Clean Air Act Title V operating permits, Clean Water Act NPDES permits, and RCRA hazardous waste generator permits. Service Provider shall prepare and file renewal applications, respond to agency information requests, and coordinate permit modifications as necessary.

> \(b\) **OSHA Compliance Support.** Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) compliance support for the Pittsburgh and Greenville facilities, including safety audits and inspections, training program management (HAZCOM, lockout/tagout, confined space, fall protection), incident investigation and reporting (OSHA 300 logs), and safety program development and implementation.

> \(c\) **EPA Reporting.** Preparation and filing of reports required by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for the Greenville and Monterrey facilities, including Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) reports, RCRA Biennial Reports, Clean Air Act emissions inventories, and any other required environmental reports. For the Monterrey facility, Service Provider shall prepare corresponding reports required by Mexico\'s Secretaría de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (SEMARNAT) and relevant state environmental agencies.

> \(d\) **Environmental Monitoring and Testing.** Coordination of ongoing environmental monitoring and testing activities at the Greenville and Pittsburgh facilities, including air emissions monitoring, wastewater sampling and analysis, groundwater monitoring (as applicable), and stormwater management program compliance.

> \(e\) **Regulatory Filing Preparation.** Preparation of regulatory filings, registrations, and submissions required by Governmental Authorities in connection with the Business\'s manufacturing operations, including chemical substance registrations under TSCA (Toxic Substances Control Act) and any required updates to existing registrations.
