4\. Replacement of any Key Personnel individual, whether due to voluntary resignation, termination for cause, disability, or other reason, shall be governed by Section 4.3 of this Agreement.
*\[End of Schedules\]*
*\[End of Agreement\]*
**Position**

**Target**                          **MUTUAL** waiver of all consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, and indirect damages (including lost profits, lost revenue, loss of business opportunity, and diminution in value). Exceptions: (i) breaches of confidentiality, (ii) IP infringement, (iii) third-party claim indemnification.
**Fallback**                        Firm position. Accept narrow additional carve-outs (willful misconduct, fraud). **Never accept a non-mutual waiver.**

**Critical Note:** The waiver must be **mutual** --- both parties waive claims against the other. A unilateral waiver (where only Service Recipient waives) is insufficient because it leaves Service Provider exposed to potentially unlimited consequential damages claims. As service provider, Polaris\'s consequential damages exposure (e.g., claims for business interruption, lost contracts, or supply chain disruption) could vastly exceed the TSA fee value. The mutual waiver limits both parties to direct damages.
**[5.3 Indemnification]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Recipient indemnifies Service Provider against all third-party claims arising from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance upon Services, except to the extent caused by Service Provider\'s **gross negligence or willful misconduct**. Service Provider\'s indemnification limited to third-party claims arising from its gross negligence or willful misconduct. All indemnification subject to the aggregate cap in Section 5.1.
**Fallback**                        Accept proportionate fault standard. Maintain gross negligence/willful misconduct threshold for Service Provider indemnification.
**[Section 6: Intellectual Property and Data]{.underline}**
**[6.1 IP Ownership]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          All Service Provider IP (proprietary technology, tools, methodologies, templates, software, systems, know-how, and processes) remains the **sole and exclusive property** of Service Provider. **No license, sublicense, right, or interest** granted to Service Recipient. Access ceases immediately upon expiration or termination.

**Fallback**                        **Firm position. No license grant is acceptable.** If buyer requires specific tools post-transition, address through a separate, independently negotiated license agreement with appropriate restrictions and compensation.
**Key Negotiation Points:**
> • Reject any license grant --- including non-exclusive, limited, or term-limited licenses --- to Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, templates, or know-how.

> • **Specifically reject** language granting *\"perpetual,\" \"irrevocable,\"* or *\"royalty-free\"* licenses. Such language permanently divests Polaris of exclusive control over its proprietary operational IP.
> • Service Recipient receives no right to use, access, copy, modify, reverse engineer, or create derivative works of any Service Provider IP outside of receiving the Services during the Term.

> • Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, and know-how have been developed over decades and are deployed across all four operating divisions. Any license to a buyer could compromise Polaris\'s competitive position and the value of these assets across Polaris\'s entire enterprise.
**[6.2 Data Ownership and Confidentiality]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Provider Data (all data, databases, and information systems owned or operated by Polaris) remains Polaris\'s confidential property. Buyer Data (data relating exclusively to the divested business, generated after Closing) is owned by Service Recipient. Service Provider will cooperate in transferring Buyer Data upon termination. Service Provider systems (including SAP S/4HANA ERP), network infrastructure, and cybersecurity tools remain Service Provider property.

**Fallback**                        Accept reasonable data separation and migration obligations. Maintain ownership of all pre-Closing data, system-level data, and Service Provider proprietary information.
**[6.3 Cross-Border Data Privacy (Mexico / LFPDPPP)]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Where Services involve processing personal data of individuals in Mexico (e.g., payroll, HR, benefits for the Monterrey facility), the TSA must include LFPDPPP-compliant provisions addressing: (i) data controller/processor allocation (Service Recipient as controller, Service Provider as processor), (ii) data processing agreement or equivalent contractual terms, (iii) cross-border data transfer consent mechanisms (privacy notices and consent from Mexican employees), (iv) data security obligations, and (v) breach notification requirements.

**Fallback**                        At minimum, include a general provision requiring compliance with all applicable data privacy laws, expressly referencing the LFPDPPP, and allocate responsibility for obtaining necessary employee consents.

**Critical Note:** The TSA must not reference only U.S. data privacy laws. Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (*Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares*) imposes distinct requirements including mandatory privacy notices (*avisos de privacidad*), consent obligations, and cross-border transfer restrictions. Failure to address these requirements in the TSA exposes both parties to enforcement risk by Mexico\'s INAI (*Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Información y Protección de Datos Personales*).
**[Section 7: Personnel]{.underline}**
**[7.1 Staffing Discretion]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Provider has **sole discretion** over staffing, assignment, reassignment, and replacement of all service-providing personnel, including the right to reassign, promote, transfer, or terminate any individual. Service Provider shall maintain reasonably qualified staff sufficient to meet the applicable service standard.

**Fallback**                        Accept obligation to provide Service Recipient **15 business days\' advance written notice** before reassigning or replacing personnel on a mutually agreed list, together with obligation to assign a reasonably qualified replacement. Reassignment/replacement decisions remain within Service Provider\'s **sole discretion** --- no consent requirement.
**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • Do not accept \"Key Personnel\" provisions requiring Service Recipient\'s prior written consent for reassignment or replacement of named individuals. Such provisions undermine Polaris\'s operational flexibility, create potential employment law complications (employees cannot be contractually \"locked\" to a specific assignment by a third party), and give the buyer undue influence over Polaris\'s internal HR decisions.
> • Polaris must retain the ability to manage its workforce across all four divisions without requiring third-party approval.
**[7.2 Non-Solicitation of Service Provider Personnel]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          During the Term and for **12 months** following termination/expiration, Service Recipient shall not solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any Polaris employee who provided Services, without Polaris\'s prior written consent. Applies to all service-providing employees (not limited to any Key Personnel list). Exceptions: (i) general solicitations not targeting Service Provider personnel, (ii) individuals terminated by Service Provider without cause.
**Fallback**                        Reduce post-termination period to 6 months (absolute minimum). Maintain restriction during the Term.

**Critical Note:** The TSA must include a non-solicitation covenant. Without one, the buyer can cherry-pick Polaris\'s most effective employees --- who gain deep familiarity with the buyer\'s operations through the TSA engagement --- depleting Polaris\'s workforce and undermining both TSA performance and Polaris\'s ability to serve its remaining businesses. This provision is a high-priority negotiation item.
**[Section 8: Insurance]{.underline}**
**[8.1 Service Recipient Insurance Requirements]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Recipient shall maintain throughout the Term (and for 12 months following expiration/termination): (a) **CGL: \$5M per occurrence / \$5M aggregate**; (b) **Umbrella/Excess: \$5M**; (c) **Workers\' Comp: statutory limits**. Service Provider named as **additional insured** under CGL and Umbrella. All policies include **waiver of subrogation** in favor of Service Provider. Certificates of insurance within 10 business days of Closing and annually thereafter.

**Fallback**                        Accept \$3M CGL and \$3M Umbrella as absolute minimums. **Never** accept CGL below \$3M, waive the umbrella requirement, or omit the additional insured endorsement.

Adequate insurance requirements protect Polaris against claims arising from the buyer\'s operations and use of Polaris\'s services and systems. Given the industrial nature of the divested businesses (coatings, chemicals, manufacturing), the risk profile warrants robust coverage. The additional insured endorsement is particularly important as it provides Polaris with direct rights under the buyer\'s policies.
**[Section 9: Audit Rights]{.underline}**
**[9.1 Service Recipient Audit Rights]{.underline}**
**Position**
**Target**                          Service Recipient may audit Service Provider\'s fee-related books and records subject to the following parameters:
**Parameter**              **Target Position**                                                                                                    **Fallback Position**
**Frequency**              Once per 12-month period                                                                                               Twice per TSA term (not twice per calendar year)
**Notice**                 30 business days\' prior written notice                                                                                20 business days\' notice (minimum)
**Timing**                 During Service Provider\'s normal business hours                                                                       Same

**Cost**                   At Service Recipient\'s sole expense                                                                                   Same; never accept audit at Service Provider\'s expense as default
**Scope**                  Fee-related records only; excludes proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, and unrelated personnel records   Same; maintain scope limitations
**Confidentiality**        All audit results confidential; no disclosure to third parties                                                         Same
**Overcharge Threshold**   If overcharge exceeds 5% for audited period, Service Provider reimburses overcharge and reasonable audit costs         Same

**Key Negotiation Points:** Excessive or frequent audits are disruptive to Polaris\'s operations. Requiring Polaris to bear audit costs as a default incentivizes frivolous audits. Short notice periods do not allow adequate preparation time and may result in incomplete responses that are then characterized as non-cooperation.
**[Section 10: Force Majeure]{.underline}**
**[10.1 Force Majeure Events]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Standard force majeure clause excusing nonperformance caused by events beyond reasonable control (natural disasters, pandemics, acts of war/terrorism, government actions, embargoes, sanctions, strikes, power failures, internet/telecom outages, cyberattacks). Affected party must provide prompt notice and use commercially reasonable mitigation efforts. Obligations suspended (not terminated) during the event. **Termination trigger: if force majeure continues for 90+ consecutive days**, either party may terminate affected Service(s) without penalty.
**Fallback**                        Accept 120-day trigger as maximum. **Never agree to a force majeure clause without a termination trigger.**

A force majeure clause without a termination trigger could leave Polaris obligated to resume services indefinitely after the event ends, regardless of how long the interruption lasted or how much circumstances have changed. The termination trigger provides both parties with a defined exit point.
**[Section 11: Governing Law and Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**
**[11.1 Governing Law]{.underline}**
**Position**
**Target**                          **Commonwealth of Pennsylvania** law, without regard to conflicts-of-law principles.
**Fallback**                        Accept **Delaware** law if the APA is governed by Delaware law. Do not accept the Service Recipient\'s home-state law.

Polaris is headquartered in Pittsburgh. The majority of service-providing personnel are Pennsylvania-based. Pennsylvania law is most familiar to Polaris\'s in-house legal team and outside counsel (Whitfield & Crane LLP). Home-state governing law is a standard and reasonable position for the service provider.
**[11.2 Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Three-step process: **(1) Escalation** to designated senior executives (CFO or General Counsel level) --- 15 business day resolution period; **(2) Mediation** (optional, non-binding); **(3) Binding arbitration** administered by **AAA** under Commercial Arbitration Rules, in **Pittsburgh, PA**, before a single arbitrator with relevant industry experience.

**Fallback**                        Accept arbitration in a neutral location (New York or Philadelphia). Accept three-arbitrator panel for disputes exceeding \$5M. **Do not accept litigation as a dispute resolution mechanism.**
**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • **Arbitration is strongly preferred over litigation.** Reasons: (a) confidentiality --- TSA disputes involve proprietary service-level and cost information; (b) speed; (c) arbitrators with industry expertise; (d) limited discovery reduces burden on Polaris; (e) Pittsburgh venue is convenient for Polaris\'s personnel and counsel.

> • Do not accept litigation in the buyer\'s home jurisdiction. State-court litigation creates home-court advantage for the buyer, exposes disputes to public dockets, and subjects Polaris to potentially unfavorable local procedural rules.
**[Section 12: Cross-Border Considerations (Mexico / Monterrey Facility)]{.underline}**
**[12.1 IMMEX Program Compliance]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Where the divested business includes a facility operating under Mexico\'s IMMEX program, the TSA must address: (i) allocation of responsibility for maintaining IMMEX certification during the transition (buyer bears primary responsibility as new operator; Polaris may provide specified transition services such as customs brokerage and import/export documentation); (ii) Polaris\'s obligation, if any, to assist with IMMEX certification transfer or renewal; (iii) compliance with all IMMEX requirements (temporary importation of materials, recordkeeping, periodic reporting to Mexico\'s Secretaría de Economía); (iv) liability allocation for IMMEX non-compliance during the transition.

**Fallback**                        Polaris will provide commercially reasonable IMMEX transition assistance. Polaris assumes no liability for buyer\'s failure to obtain or maintain its own IMMEX certification post-Closing.

**Critical Note:** IMMEX non-compliance can result in significant penalties, loss of duty deferral benefits, and operational disruption at the Monterrey facility. Clear allocation of IMMEX responsibilities in the TSA is essential. A TSA that omits IMMEX provisions entirely creates dangerous ambiguity regarding which party bears compliance responsibility during the transition.
**[12.2 Mexican Data Privacy (LFPDPPP) --- Cross-Reference]{.underline}**

See Section 6.3 above. Any TSA involving the Monterrey facility must include LFPDPPP-compliant data privacy provisions for processing Mexican employees\' personal data. Additionally, consider whether Mexican employment law (*Ley Federal del Trabajo*) imposes restrictions on the provision of HR or payroll services by a non-employer entity (Polaris) on behalf of the new employer (buyer), and structure service delivery accordingly to avoid inadvertent co-employment risk.
**[Section 13: Miscellaneous Playbook Provisions]{.underline}**
**[13.1 Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Mutual confidentiality obligations with a three (3) year survival period following expiration or termination. Standard carve-outs for legal compulsion, publicly available information, independent development, and prior knowledge. These are generally market-standard provisions and should not require significant negotiation.
**[13.2 Assignment]{.underline}**

Neither party may assign the TSA without the prior written consent of the other party, except in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of substantially all assets. This is a standard provision and should not require significant negotiation.
**[13.3 Notices]{.underline}**

All notices shall be in writing and delivered to the designated addresses. For Polaris: 1200 Commonwealth Avenue, Suite 3000, Pittsburgh, PA 15222, Attention: General Counsel (Sharon M. Petrosian), with a copy to Whitfield & Crane LLP, 600 Grant Street, Suite 4800, Pittsburgh, PA 15219, Attention: Victoria S. Andersen. Notices shall be effective upon receipt.
**[13.4 Invoicing Cadence]{.underline}**
Monthly invoicing by Service Provider within fifteen (15) business days after the end of each calendar month is standard and acceptable across all Polaris TSAs.
**[Appendix A: Quick Reference --- Issue Spotting Checklist]{.underline}**

The following checklist summarizes each playbook position and identifies red flags to look for when reviewing a buyer\'s draft TSA. The reviewing attorney should compare the buyer\'s draft against each row and flag all deviations for discussion.

**Issue Category**                       **Polaris Target Position**                                                                                                     **Red Flags in Buyer\'s Draft**                                                                                                       **APA Constraint**

**Service Standard**                     12-month lookback; \"substantially consistent with\"; no best-practices overlay                                                 Extended lookback (e.g., 24 months); \"equal to or better than\"; \"industry best practices\"; \"best efforts\"                       APA service standard controls if specified

**Liability Cap**                        Trailing 12-month fees actually paid                                                                                            Total-fee caps; multiples of total fees (e.g., 200%); fixed dollar amounts exceeding trailing 12-month calculation                    APA §7.12(d) mandates trailing 12-month cap

**Consequential Damages**                Mutual waiver (both parties waive)                                                                                              One-way waiver (only Service Recipient waives); missing waiver entirely; non-mutual carve-outs                                        ---

**Term**                                 18-month hard stop; no automatic renewal; extensions by mutual consent only at cost-plus-15%                                    Automatic renewal clauses; extension options exercisable by one party; terms exceeding 18 months without mutual consent               APA §7.12 mandates 18-month maximum

**Termination Notice**                   90 days for individual service termination                                                                                      Notice periods exceeding 90 days (e.g., 120 days); asymmetric notice periods favoring buyer                                           APA §7.12(c) mandates 90-day notice

**Personnel / Staffing**                 Sole discretion over staffing decisions                                                                                         Key Personnel lists with consent requirements; restrictions on reassignment; buyer approval for replacements                          ---

**Fee Markup**                           Uniform cost-plus-10% across all service categories                                                                             Per-category markups exceeding 10%; non-uniform markups; markups applied inconsistently                                               APA §7.12(b) mandates 10% cap

**Audit Rights**                         Once per 12-month period; buyer\'s expense; 30 business days\' notice; fee records only                                         Increased frequency (e.g., twice per year); audit at seller\'s expense; short notice (e.g., 10 days); expanded scope                  ---

**Governing Law / Dispute Resolution**   Pennsylvania law; AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh                                                                                 Buyer\'s home-state law (e.g., Ohio); litigation in buyer\'s home-state courts; unfavorable venue                                     ---

**IP Ownership**                         No license; all Service Provider IP remains Polaris\'s exclusive property                                                       Any license grant (especially perpetual, irrevocable, or royalty-free); rights to tools, methodologies, templates, or know-how        ---

**Non-Solicitation**                     12-month post-service restriction on hiring Polaris personnel                                                                   Missing non-solicitation provision entirely; narrowly scoped restriction (e.g., Key Personnel only); short duration                   ---

**Insurance**                            \$5M CGL + \$5M umbrella + additional insured endorsement + waiver of subrogation                                               Lower limits (e.g., \$2M CGL); missing umbrella requirement; no additional insured endorsement; no waiver of subrogation              ---

**Cross-Border (Mexico)**                IMMEX compliance allocation + LFPDPPP data privacy provisions                                                                   Omission of Mexico-specific provisions entirely; failure to address IMMEX certification responsibility; no LFPDPPP compliance terms   ---

**Termination Assistance**               60-day wind-down period at cost-plus-15%; includes knowledge transfer, data migration, cooperation with replacement providers   Missing termination assistance provision entirely; undefined wind-down obligations; no pricing for wind-down services                 ---

**Change Orders**                        Written change order signed by both parties; cost-plus-15%; acceptance at Polaris\'s sole discretion                            Missing change order procedure; informal scope expansion mechanisms; no pricing for out-of-scope work                                 ---

**Payment Terms**                        Net 30; late interest at 1.5%/month; undisputed portions paid regardless of disputes                                            Vague language (\"commercially reasonable time\"); no late interest provision; no obligation to pay undisputed amounts                ---

**Force Majeure**                        90-day termination trigger if force majeure event persists                                                                      Missing termination trigger; no defined exit mechanism for prolonged force majeure events                                             ---
**END OF PLAYBOOK**
For questions, contact Sharon M. Petrosian, General Counsel, Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc.
Next scheduled review: July 2025

101: *\[Article VII of the Agreement contains covenants of the parties from signing through Closing and certain post-Closing covenants. Sections 7.1 through 7.11 address, among other things, conduct of the Business pending the Closing, access to information and properties, regulatory filings and approvals, certain employee matters, and other pre-Closing covenants, and are not reproduced herein. Section 7.12, which governs the Transition Services Agreement, is reproduced in full below. Sections 7.13 through 7.18 address non-competition and non-solicitation covenants, public announcements, tax matters, further assurances, and other post-Closing covenants, and are not reproduced herein.\]*
102: 
103: **[Section 7.12 --- Transition Services Agreement]{.underline}**
104: 
105: **Section 7.12(a) --- Obligation to Enter into TSA**
106: 
107: At or prior to the Closing, Seller and Buyer shall negotiate in good faith and enter into a Transition Services Agreement, on commercially reasonable terms and conditions, pursuant to which Seller shall provide, or cause to be provided, to Buyer (or its applicable Affiliates) the Transition Services described in Exhibit H hereto for a transition period following the Closing Date (the \"**Transition Period**\"). The purpose of the Transition Services Agreement is to facilitate an orderly transition of the Business from Seller to Buyer and to enable Buyer to establish independent operational capability with respect to the functions and services described in Exhibit H.
108: 
109: The Transition Period shall commence on the Closing Date and shall not exceed eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Maximum TSA Term**\"). Each individual Transition Service shall be provided for the period specified in Exhibit H with respect to such Transition Service, which period shall in no event exceed the Maximum TSA Term.
110: 
111: For the avoidance of doubt, the Transition Period shall expire no later than the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to extend the Transition Period for any individual Transition Service, provided that no such extension shall exceed an additional six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for any individual Transition Service. Any such extension shall be documented in a written amendment to the Transition Services Agreement executed by both parties. No automatic renewal or extension mechanism shall be included in the Transition Services Agreement.
112: 
113: The Transition Services shall be provided in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services were provided to the Business during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the Closing Date. Seller shall allocate sufficient resources and qualified personnel to provide the Transition Services in accordance with the foregoing standard throughout the Transition Period.
114: 
115: **Section 7.12(b) --- Service Fees**
116: 
117: All fees payable by Buyer to Seller under the Transition Services Agreement for the Transition Services (the \"**TSA Fees**\") shall be calculated on a cost-plus basis, reflecting the Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost (as defined in Section 1.1) of providing each Transition Service, plus a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost.
118: 
119: The estimated Fully-Loaded Cost and estimated monthly TSA Fees for each category of Transition Services are set forth in Exhibit H. Such estimates are based on Seller\'s actual cost experience for the twelve (12) months ended December 31, 2024, and shall be subject to adjustment in the Transition Services Agreement to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period, provided that any such adjustment shall be calculated in accordance with the Fully-Loaded Cost definition and shall not exceed the estimated amounts set forth in Exhibit H by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent.
120: 
121: In no event shall the markup applied to any category of Transition Service exceed ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost for such category. This limitation shall apply to each category of Transition Service individually and not solely on an aggregate or blended basis across all categories.
122: 
123: Any fees for services that are not described in Exhibit H but that are requested by Buyer and agreed to by Seller in writing (\"**Additional Services**\") shall be priced on terms to be mutually agreed by the parties, which pricing may include a markup in excess of ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with a good faith estimate of the Fully-Loaded Cost and proposed markup for any Additional Service prior to the commencement of such Additional Service.
124: 
125: **Section 7.12(c) --- Termination of Individual Services**
126: 
127: Buyer or Seller may terminate any individual Transition Service upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other party, specifying the Transition Service to be terminated and the effective date of such termination. Such notice shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 12.1 of this Agreement.
128: 
129: Upon termination of any individual Transition Service, Buyer\'s obligation to pay TSA Fees with respect to such terminated Transition Service shall cease as of the effective date of termination, subject to Buyer\'s obligation to pay all TSA Fees accrued through such effective date and to reimburse Seller for any non-cancelable costs or commitments that Seller incurred prior to receipt of the termination notice in reasonable reliance on the continuation of such Transition Service, provided that Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate such non-cancelable costs.
130: 
131: Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Transition Services Agreement provides for a notice period different from the ninety (90) day period specified in this Section 7.12(c), the notice period set forth in this Agreement shall control. The parties acknowledge and agree that this Section 7.12(c) establishes the minimum and maximum notice period applicable to the termination of individual Transition Services, and any provision in the Transition Services Agreement purporting to require a longer or shorter notice period shall be of no force or effect.
132: 
133: **Section 7.12(d) --- Limitation of Liability**
134: 
135: The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that the aggregate liability of the Service Provider (and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents) to the Service Recipient under or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, whether arising in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient to the Service Provider during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient (the \"**TSA Liability Cap**\").
136: 
137: For purposes of calculating the TSA Liability Cap during the first twelve (12) months of the Transition Period, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated based on the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient from the Closing Date through the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient. Thereafter, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated on a rolling twelve (12) month basis, measured from the date of assertion of the applicable claim and looking back twelve (12) months from such date.
138: 
139: The limitation set forth in this Section 7.12(d) shall not apply to:
140: 
141: > \(i\) claims arising from a party\'s fraud or willful misconduct;
142: >
143: > \(ii\) a party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations under the Transition Services Agreement; or
144: >
145: > \(iii\) a party\'s indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims arising out of the provision or receipt of Transition Services, to the extent such third-party claims result from the indemnifying party\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.
146: 
147: In no event shall either party be liable to the other party for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages arising out of or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, regardless of whether such damages are based on contract, tort, strict liability, or any other theory, and regardless of whether such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages; provided, however, that this sentence shall not limit the liability of a party with respect to third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under the Transition Services Agreement.
148: 
149: The parties acknowledge and agree that the foregoing limitations on liability reflect the parties\' agreement regarding the allocation of risk under the Transition Services Agreement, and that neither party would have entered into this Agreement without such limitations.
150: 
151: **Section 7.12(e) --- Cooperation**
152: 
153: During the Transition Period, Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish its own capability to perform the Transition Services independently and to reduce its reliance on Seller for the provision of such Transition Services as promptly as reasonably practicable. Buyer shall dedicate appropriate internal resources, including qualified personnel and financial resources, to the transition effort and shall develop and implement a transition plan in consultation with Seller.
154: 
155: Seller shall cooperate in good faith with Buyer\'s efforts to transition the Transition Services to Buyer\'s own systems, personnel, and third-party providers. Such cooperation shall include reasonable knowledge transfer, documentation of processes and procedures, and making Seller\'s personnel reasonably available for consultations during normal business hours.
156: 
157: Nothing in this Section 7.12 or the Transition Services Agreement shall require Seller to:
158: 
159: > \(i\) maintain any employee in employment or any contractor engagement solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services;
160: >
161: > \(ii\) acquire, license, or maintain any hardware, software, or other technology solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services, except to the extent that Seller was licensing or maintaining such technology for the benefit of the Business as of the Closing Date and the cost of such license or maintenance is included in the Fully-Loaded Cost;
162: >
163: > \(iii\) provide any Transition Service in a manner that would require Seller to violate any applicable Law or breach any contractual obligation to a third party; or
164: >
165: > \(iv\) disclose any trade secrets, proprietary information, or confidential business information of Seller that does not relate to the Business.
166: 
167: **Section 7.12(f) --- Service Standard; No Prioritization**
168: 
169: The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that Seller shall provide the Transition Services in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality at which such services (or substantially similar services) were provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date. The parties acknowledge that Seller\'s historical practices, methodologies, systems, and resource levels as applied to the Business during such twelve (12) month period shall serve as the benchmark for the required level of service under the Transition Services Agreement.
170: 
171: Nothing in the Transition Services Agreement shall obligate Seller to provide Transition Services at a level of quality, timeliness, or responsiveness that exceeds the level provided to the Business during such twelve (12) month period, or to prioritize the provision of Transition Services over services that Seller provides for its own account, for its retained business divisions, or for its other business units. Seller shall not be required to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices in connection with the provision of Transition Services that were not in use with respect to the Business during such twelve (12) month period.
172: 
173: The parties acknowledge and agree that Seller is not a professional services provider and that the Transition Services are being provided on an accommodation basis to facilitate the orderly transition of the Business to Buyer. Accordingly, the parties agree that the standard of care applicable to the provision of Transition Services shall be measured solely by reference to Seller\'s historical performance with respect to the Business and shall not be measured against any external industry standard, best-practice benchmark, or professional services standard.
174: 
175: **Section 7.12(g) --- Cross-Border Services**
176: 
177: To the extent that any Transition Services are provided in connection with the operations of the Monterrey Facility or involve the processing of personal data of employees located in Mexico, the Transition Services Agreement shall include commercially reasonable provisions to ensure compliance with applicable Mexican Law, including:
178: 
179: > \(i\) the IMMEX Program requirements applicable to the Monterrey Facility, including provisions addressing the maintenance of the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification, the allocation of responsibility for IMMEX reporting obligations during the Transition Period, and compliance with applicable customs and trade requirements; and
180: >

**[Section 7.12 --- Transition Services Agreement]{.underline}**
**Section 7.12(a) --- Obligation to Enter into TSA**

At or prior to the Closing, Seller and Buyer shall negotiate in good faith and enter into a Transition Services Agreement, on commercially reasonable terms and conditions, pursuant to which Seller shall provide, or cause to be provided, to Buyer (or its applicable Affiliates) the Transition Services described in Exhibit H hereto for a transition period following the Closing Date (the \"**Transition Period**\"). The purpose of the Transition Services Agreement is to facilitate an orderly transition of the Business from Seller to Buyer and to enable Buyer to establish independent operational capability with respect to the functions and services described in Exhibit H.

The Transition Period shall commence on the Closing Date and shall not exceed eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Maximum TSA Term**\"). Each individual Transition Service shall be provided for the period specified in Exhibit H with respect to such Transition Service, which period shall in no event exceed the Maximum TSA Term.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Transition Period shall expire no later than the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to extend the Transition Period for any individual Transition Service, provided that no such extension shall exceed an additional six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for any individual Transition Service. Any such extension shall be documented in a written amendment to the Transition Services Agreement executed by both parties. No automatic renewal or extension mechanism shall be included in the Transition Services Agreement.

The Transition Services shall be provided in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services were provided to the Business during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the Closing Date. Seller shall allocate sufficient resources and qualified personnel to provide the Transition Services in accordance with the foregoing standard throughout the Transition Period.
**Section 7.12(b) --- Service Fees**

All fees payable by Buyer to Seller under the Transition Services Agreement for the Transition Services (the \"**TSA Fees**\") shall be calculated on a cost-plus basis, reflecting the Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost (as defined in Section 1.1) of providing each Transition Service, plus a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost.

The estimated Fully-Loaded Cost and estimated monthly TSA Fees for each category of Transition Services are set forth in Exhibit H. Such estimates are based on Seller\'s actual cost experience for the twelve (12) months ended December 31, 2024, and shall be subject to adjustment in the Transition Services Agreement to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period, provided that any such adjustment shall be calculated in accordance with the Fully-Loaded Cost definition and shall not exceed the estimated amounts set forth in Exhibit H by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent.

In no event shall the markup applied to any category of Transition Service exceed ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost for such category. This limitation shall apply to each category of Transition Service individually and not solely on an aggregate or blended basis across all categories.

Any fees for services that are not described in Exhibit H but that are requested by Buyer and agreed to by Seller in writing (\"**Additional Services**\") shall be priced on terms to be mutually agreed by the parties, which pricing may include a markup in excess of ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with a good faith estimate of the Fully-Loaded Cost and proposed markup for any Additional Service prior to the commencement of such Additional Service.
**Section 7.12(c) --- Termination of Individual Services**

Buyer or Seller may terminate any individual Transition Service upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other party, specifying the Transition Service to be terminated and the effective date of such termination. Such notice shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 12.1 of this Agreement.

Upon termination of any individual Transition Service, Buyer\'s obligation to pay TSA Fees with respect to such terminated Transition Service shall cease as of the effective date of termination, subject to Buyer\'s obligation to pay all TSA Fees accrued through such effective date and to reimburse Seller for any non-cancelable costs or commitments that Seller incurred prior to receipt of the termination notice in reasonable reliance on the continuation of such Transition Service, provided that Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate such non-cancelable costs.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Transition Services Agreement provides for a notice period different from the ninety (90) day period specified in this Section 7.12(c), the notice period set forth in this Agreement shall control. The parties acknowledge and agree that this Section 7.12(c) establishes the minimum and maximum notice period applicable to the termination of individual Transition Services, and any provision in the Transition Services Agreement purporting to require a longer or shorter notice period shall be of no force or effect.
**Section 7.12(d) --- Limitation of Liability**

The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that the aggregate liability of the Service Provider (and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents) to the Service Recipient under or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, whether arising in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient to the Service Provider during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient (the \"**TSA Liability Cap**\").

For purposes of calculating the TSA Liability Cap during the first twelve (12) months of the Transition Period, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated based on the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient from the Closing Date through the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient. Thereafter, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated on a rolling twelve (12) month basis, measured from the date of assertion of the applicable claim and looking back twelve (12) months from such date.
The limitation set forth in this Section 7.12(d) shall not apply to:
> \(i\) claims arising from a party\'s fraud or willful misconduct;
> \(ii\) a party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations under the Transition Services Agreement; or

> \(iii\) a party\'s indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims arising out of the provision or receipt of Transition Services, to the extent such third-party claims result from the indemnifying party\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.

In no event shall either party be liable to the other party for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages arising out of or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, regardless of whether such damages are based on contract, tort, strict liability, or any other theory, and regardless of whether such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages; provided, however, that this sentence shall not limit the liability of a party with respect to third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under the Transition Services Agreement.

The parties acknowledge and agree that the foregoing limitations on liability reflect the parties\' agreement regarding the allocation of risk under the Transition Services Agreement, and that neither party would have entered into this Agreement without such limitations.
**Section 7.12(e) --- Cooperation**

During the Transition Period, Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish its own capability to perform the Transition Services independently and to reduce its reliance on Seller for the provision of such Transition Services as promptly as reasonably practicable. Buyer shall dedicate appropriate internal resources, including qualified personnel and financial resources, to the transition effort and shall develop and implement a transition plan in consultation with Seller.

Seller shall cooperate in good faith with Buyer\'s efforts to transition the Transition Services to Buyer\'s own systems, personnel, and third-party providers. Such cooperation shall include reasonable knowledge transfer, documentation of processes and procedures, and making Seller\'s personnel reasonably available for consultations during normal business hours.
Nothing in this Section 7.12 or the Transition Services Agreement shall require Seller to:
> \(i\) maintain any employee in employment or any contractor engagement solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services;

> \(ii\) acquire, license, or maintain any hardware, software, or other technology solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services, except to the extent that Seller was licensing or maintaining such technology for the benefit of the Business as of the Closing Date and the cost of such license or maintenance is included in the Fully-Loaded Cost;
> \(iii\) provide any Transition Service in a manner that would require Seller to violate any applicable Law or breach any contractual obligation to a third party; or
> \(iv\) disclose any trade secrets, proprietary information, or confidential business information of Seller that does not relate to the Business.
**Section 7.12(f) --- Service Standard; No Prioritization**

The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that Seller shall provide the Transition Services in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality at which such services (or substantially similar services) were provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date. The parties acknowledge that Seller\'s historical practices, methodologies, systems, and resource levels as applied to the Business during such twelve (12) month period shall serve as the benchmark for the required level of service under the Transition Services Agreement.

Nothing in the Transition Services Agreement shall obligate Seller to provide Transition Services at a level of quality, timeliness, or responsiveness that exceeds the level provided to the Business during such twelve (12) month period, or to prioritize the provision of Transition Services over services that Seller provides for its own account, for its retained business divisions, or for its other business units. Seller shall not be required to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices in connection with the provision of Transition Services that were not in use with respect to the Business during such twelve (12) month period.

The parties acknowledge and agree that Seller is not a professional services provider and that the Transition Services are being provided on an accommodation basis to facilitate the orderly transition of the Business to Buyer. Accordingly, the parties agree that the standard of care applicable to the provision of Transition Services shall be measured solely by reference to Seller\'s historical performance with respect to the Business and shall not be measured against any external industry standard, best-practice benchmark, or professional services standard.
**Section 7.12(g) --- Cross-Border Services**

To the extent that any Transition Services are provided in connection with the operations of the Monterrey Facility or involve the processing of personal data of employees located in Mexico, the Transition Services Agreement shall include commercially reasonable provisions to ensure compliance with applicable Mexican Law, including:

> \(i\) the IMMEX Program requirements applicable to the Monterrey Facility, including provisions addressing the maintenance of the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification, the allocation of responsibility for IMMEX reporting obligations during the Transition Period, and compliance with applicable customs and trade requirements; and

> \(ii\) Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (*Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares*) and its Regulations, including provisions addressing the lawful basis for the transfer and processing of personal data of Monterrey Facility employees, the implementation of appropriate privacy notices (*avisos de privacidad*), and the establishment of adequate data protection safeguards.

Seller and Buyer shall cooperate in good faith to determine the appropriate allocation of responsibilities under the IMMEX Program during the Transition Period, including with respect to the maintenance of the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification, the timely filing of all required IMMEX reports, and the management of temporary importation records. The parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the transition of IMMEX Program obligations from Seller to Buyer is completed in a manner that avoids any lapse in the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification or any violation of applicable Mexican customs Law.

**TRANSITION SERVICE CATEGORY DESCRIPTIONS**

The following sets forth the categories of Transition Services to be provided by Seller to Buyer pursuant to the Transition Services Agreement to be entered into in accordance with Section 7.12 of the Asset Purchase Agreement, together with a general description of each category, estimated personnel requirements, and estimated Fully-Loaded Cost.
**General Notes:**

All estimated costs set forth below are based on Seller\'s actual cost experience for the twelve (12) months ended December 31, 2024, and are subject to adjustment in the Transition Services Agreement to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period. The markup applied to each category shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost, as provided in Section 7.12(b) of the Agreement.

The Transition Services shall be provided in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality at which such services were provided to the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date, as provided in Sections 7.12(a) and 7.12(f) of the Agreement.

All FTE counts set forth below are estimates based on current staffing levels and may be adjusted by Seller in its reasonable discretion, provided that Seller shall at all times allocate sufficient resources to meet the applicable service standard.
**[Category 1 --- Financial Reporting & Accounting]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** General ledger maintenance and posting for the Business, including all journal entries, account reconciliations, and period-end close activities; accounts payable processing and payment execution, including invoice review, approval workflows, vendor payment processing, and check or wire disbursement; accounts receivable invoicing and collection support, including customer invoice generation, cash application, aging analysis, and collection activity coordination; monthly financial close activities and reconciliations, including intercompany eliminations and balance sheet reconciliations; management reporting, including standard monthly financial reporting packages (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement, and variance analysis); and ad hoc financial analysis support reasonably requested by Buyer in connection with the operation of the Business.

**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately twenty-two (22) full-time equivalent personnel, including personnel in general accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and financial reporting functions. Specific personnel assignments shall be determined by Seller in its reasonable discretion, provided that Seller shall ensure continuity of key personnel to the extent reasonably practicable.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$185,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$203,500
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.
**[Category 2 --- Information Technology]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** Continued access to and support of Seller\'s SAP S/4HANA enterprise resource planning system for all Business-related modules (including finance and controlling, procurement and materials management, production planning and manufacturing execution, sales and distribution, and human capital management modules); network infrastructure support for the Facilities, including LAN/WAN administration, firewall management, and connectivity monitoring; cybersecurity monitoring and incident response services, including threat detection, vulnerability scanning, and security event management; email and collaboration tools administration, including Microsoft 365 platform management and user account administration; help desk support (Tier 1 and Tier 2) for Business-related IT issues; data backup and disaster recovery services, including regular backup execution, backup verification, and recovery testing; and management of Business-related IT assets, including hardware inventory tracking and end-of-life replacement coordination.

**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately thirty-one (31) full-time equivalent personnel, including ERP administrators, network engineers, cybersecurity analysts, database administrators, and help desk staff.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$340,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$374,000
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.

**Special Note:** Buyer acknowledges that Seller\'s SAP S/4HANA system is an integrated enterprise platform that serves all of Seller\'s business divisions, including the Architectural Coatings Division, the Performance Polymers Division, and Seller\'s corporate functions. Seller shall provide Buyer with access to Business-related modules and data only, and Buyer shall not access, view, or attempt to access or view any data, modules, or system components that are not related to the Business. Seller shall have no obligation to modify, customize, or develop new functionality within the SAP S/4HANA system for the benefit of Buyer, and Seller retains sole discretion over the administration, configuration, and upgrade schedule of the SAP S/4HANA system, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with reasonable advance notice of any planned system changes that would materially affect the Transition Services. Buyer\'s access to the SAP S/4HANA system shall terminate upon the earlier of (i) the expiration or termination of this Category of Transition Services or (ii) Buyer\'s successful migration to its own enterprise resource planning system.
**[Category 3 --- Human Resources]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** Payroll processing and administration for Transferred Employees during the Transition Period, including payroll calculation, payroll tax withholding and reporting (federal, state, and local), direct deposit administration, and W-2 preparation; benefits administration (medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability, and 401(k) plan) during any transition period before Buyer establishes its own benefit plans and enrolls Transferred Employees therein; HRIS system access and support, including maintenance of employee records, employee self-service portal administration, and standard HR reporting; workers\' compensation claims management and reporting; and general HR advisory support, including guidance on employment law compliance, employee relations matters, and leave of absence administration, in each case to the extent consistent with the services historically provided by Seller\'s corporate human resources function to the Business.
**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately eighteen (18) full-time equivalent personnel, including payroll specialists, benefits administrators, HRIS analysts, and HR generalists.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$125,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$137,500
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.

**Special Note Regarding Monterrey Facility:** With respect to Transferred Employees located at the Monterrey Facility, Seller shall process payroll and administer benefits in accordance with applicable Mexican Law, including the Federal Labor Law (*Ley Federal del Trabajo*) and applicable social security (*Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social*, or \"IMSS\") and housing fund (*Instituto del Fondo Nacional de la Vivienda para los Trabajadores*, or \"INFONAVIT\") requirements. The parties shall include appropriate provisions in the Transition Services Agreement to address compliance with Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (*Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares*) and its Regulations in connection with the processing of personal data of Monterrey Facility employees, including the preparation and distribution of appropriate privacy notices (*avisos de privacidad*) and the establishment of data transfer mechanisms compliant with such Law.
**[Category 4 --- Supply Chain & Procurement]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** Raw material sourcing and procurement under Seller\'s existing master supply agreements (to the extent such agreements are assignable or otherwise available for Buyer\'s benefit during the Transition Period, and subject to any required third-party consents); logistics coordination for inbound and outbound shipments, including carrier management, freight rate negotiation, and shipment tracking; warehouse management services at the shared warehouse facility located within the Pittsburgh Manufacturing Facility, including receiving, put-away, picking, packing, and shipping operations for Business-related inventory; inventory management support, including cycle counting, inventory valuation, and stock replenishment planning; and vendor relationship management during the transition to Buyer\'s own supply chain organization, including facilitating introductions between Buyer and key suppliers and assisting with the transition of purchasing relationships.
**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately fourteen (14) full-time equivalent personnel, including procurement specialists, logistics coordinators, warehouse supervisors, and inventory analysts.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$210,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$231,000
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.

**Special Note:** Buyer acknowledges that certain of Seller\'s master supply agreements contain change-of-control, assignment, or consent provisions that may require third-party consents in connection with the provision of procurement services to Buyer. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain any required consents; provided, however, that Seller shall not be required to pay any consideration to any third party, agree to any material modification of any master supply agreement, or incur any material obligation or liability in order to obtain such consents. In the event that any required consent cannot be obtained, the parties shall cooperate in good faith to identify alternative arrangements that provide Buyer with substantially equivalent access to the relevant raw materials or supplies.
**[Category 5 --- Regulatory & EHS Compliance]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** Environmental permit maintenance and compliance support for the Greenville and Monterrey Facilities, including permit renewal tracking, compliance calendar management, and regulatory agency correspondence; Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) compliance monitoring and reporting, including workplace inspection support, incident investigation, and recordkeeping; Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) reporting obligations related to the Business, including Toxic Release Inventory (TRI) reporting, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) compliance, and Clean Air Act permit reporting; workplace safety program administration, including safety training program coordination, personal protective equipment program management, and safety committee facilitation; environmental audit support, including coordination of internal and third-party environmental audits; and hazardous materials management compliance, including hazardous waste manifesting, storage area inspections, and transportation of dangerous goods compliance.
**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately eight (8) full-time equivalent personnel, including environmental compliance specialists, safety engineers, and regulatory affairs analysts.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$95,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$104,500
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.

**Special Note Regarding Monterrey Facility:** With respect to the Monterrey Facility, Regulatory & EHS Compliance services shall include support for compliance with applicable Mexican environmental standards (*Normas Oficiales Mexicanas*, or \"NOM\" standards), including NOM-001-SEMARNAT-2021 (wastewater discharge) and NOM-043-SEMARNAT-1993 (particulate emissions), and assistance with maintaining the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX Program certification. The parties shall include appropriate provisions in the Transition Services Agreement to allocate responsibility for IMMEX Program compliance during the Transition Period, including responsibility for the filing of required IMMEX reports with Mexico\'s Ministry of Economy (*Secretaría de Economía*) and the maintenance of temporary importation records required under applicable Mexican customs regulations.

**Special Note Regarding Pittsburgh Manufacturing Facility:** For the avoidance of doubt, the Pittsburgh Manufacturing Facility\'s environmental permits and compliance obligations are included in the Acquired Assets and shall be transferred to Buyer at Closing pursuant to Section 2.1. The Regulatory & EHS Compliance Transition Services with respect to the Pittsburgh Manufacturing Facility are limited to transitional compliance support to facilitate Buyer\'s assumption of direct responsibility for such permits and obligations, including assistance with permit transfer applications, compliance history documentation, and introduction to applicable regulatory agency contacts.
**[Category 6 --- Treasury & Tax]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** Cash management services for the Business during the Transition Period, including cash concentration, disbursement, and intercompany settlement through Seller\'s existing treasury management infrastructure; bank account transition support, including assistance with the establishment of Buyer\'s own bank accounts and the orderly transfer of banking relationships; sales and use tax return preparation and filing for the Business; property tax return preparation and filing for the Facilities; and support for any ongoing tax audits or inquiries related to the pre-Closing operations of the Business, including document compilation, data retrieval, and coordination with Seller\'s tax department.
**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately seven (7) full-time equivalent personnel, including treasury analysts, tax compliance specialists, and tax research analysts.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$65,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$71,500
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from docx.enum.text import WD_LINE_SPACING
from docx.enum.table import WD_ROW_HEIGHT_RULE
from docx.enum.text import WD_COLOR_INDEX
from docx.oxml.shared import OxmlElement
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path('output')
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

RED = RGBColor(0xC0,0x00,0x00)
BLUE = RGBColor(0x00,0x33,0x99)
DARK = RGBColor(0x1F,0x29,0x37)
GRAY = 'F3F4F6'
PALE_RED = 'FCE4D6'
PALE_BLUE = 'DDEBF7'
PALE_YELLOW = 'FFF2CC'
PALE_GREEN = 'E2F0D9'
BORDER = 'B7C9D6'


def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:
        tcBorders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge)
            element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag); tcBorders.append(element)
            for key, value in kwargs[edge].items():
                element.set(qn('w:{}'.format(key)), str(value))

def set_table_borders(table, color=BORDER, sz='6'):
    for row in table.rows:
        for cell in row.cells:
            set_cell_border(cell, top={'val':'single','sz':sz,'color':color}, bottom={'val':'single','sz':sz,'color':color}, left={'val':'single','sz':sz,'color':color}, right={'val':'single','sz':sz,'color':color})

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=100, bottom=80, end=100):
    tc = cell._tc; tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar'); tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top',top),('start',start),('bottom',bottom),('end',end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn(f'w:{m}'))
        if node is None: node = OxmlElement(f'w:{m}'); tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'), str(v)); node.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa')

def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); trPr.append(tblHeader)

def set_col_widths(table, widths):
    for row in table.rows:
        for idx, width in enumerate(widths):
            row.cells[idx].width = Inches(width)

def add_page_number(paragraph):
    paragraph.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
    run = paragraph.add_run('Page ')
    fldChar1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    instrText = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); instrText.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); instrText.text = 'PAGE'
    fldChar2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    run._r.append(fldChar1); run._r.append(instrText); run._r.append(fldChar2)

def setup(doc, title):
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    sec.top_margin = Inches(0.65); sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.65); sec.left_margin = Inches(0.75); sec.right_margin = Inches(0.75)
    sec.header_distance = Inches(0.3); sec.footer_distance = Inches(0.3)
    styles = doc.styles
    normal = styles['Normal']; normal.font.name = 'Arial'; normal.font.size = Pt(9.5); normal.font.color.rgb = DARK
    normal.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4); normal.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.05
    for name, size, color in [('Title',20,DARK),('Heading 1',15,DARK),('Heading 2',12,DARK),('Heading 3',10.5,DARK)]:
        st = styles[name]; st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.size=Pt(size); st.font.bold=True; st.font.color.rgb=color
        st.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(10); st.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(5)
    if 'Small Note' not in [s.name for s in styles]:
        st = styles.add_style('Small Note', WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH); st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.size=Pt(8); st.font.italic=True; st.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x55,0x55,0x55)
    if 'Redline Delete' not in [s.name for s in styles]:
        st = styles.add_style('Redline Delete', WD_STYLE_TYPE.CHARACTER); st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.color.rgb=RED; st.font.strike=True
    if 'Redline Add' not in [s.name for s in styles]:
        st = styles.add_style('Redline Add', WD_STYLE_TYPE.CHARACTER); st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.color.rgb=BLUE; st.font.underline=True
    hp = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
    hp.text = 'PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT'
    hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    hp.runs[0].font.name='Arial'; hp.runs[0].font.size=Pt(8); hp.runs[0].font.bold=True; hp.runs[0].font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x66,0x66,0x66)
    fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]; fp.text='Polaris / Trident — TSA Review  |  '; fp.runs[0].font.name='Arial'; fp.runs[0].font.size=Pt(8); fp.runs[0].font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x66,0x66,0x66); add_page_number(fp)

def add_title(doc, title, subtitle):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r=p.add_run(title); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(20); r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.color.rgb=DARK
    p2=doc.add_paragraph(); p2.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r=p2.add_run(subtitle); r.italic=True; r.font.size=Pt(11); r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0x55,0x55,0x55)
    for text in ['Prepared for: Victoria S. Andersen, Whitfield & Crane LLP','Client: Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. (Seller / Service Provider)','Draft reviewed: Trident first draft dated April 28, 2025','Review benchmark: Polaris TSA Playbook (Jan. 15, 2025) and APA §7.12 / Exhibit H']:
        p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER; r=p.add_run(text); r.font.size=Pt(9); r.font.name='Arial'
    doc.add_paragraph()

def add_note_box(doc, label, text, fill=PALE_YELLOW):
    t=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1); t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER; set_table_borders(t, color='D6B656', sz='6')
    c=t.cell(0,0); set_cell_shading(c,fill); set_cell_margins(c,100,140,100,140)
    p=c.paragraphs[0]; r=p.add_run(label+' '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=DARK; r.font.size=Pt(9)
    r=p.add_run(text); r.font.size=Pt(9)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)

def add_redline_block(doc, cid, tier, heading, draft, proposed, basis, risk, position, comment_text, citations=''):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Heading 2')
    rr=p.add_run(f'{cid} — {heading} [{tier}]'); rr.bold=True; rr.font.color.rgb=RED if tier=='CRITICAL' else (RGBColor(0xBF,0x7F,0x00) if tier=='SIGNIFICANT' else RGBColor(0x55,0x55,0x55))
    # draft deletion
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); r=p.add_run('[DELETE — draft language] '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RED; r.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    rd=p.add_run(draft); rd.font.color.rgb=RED; rd.font.strike=True; rd.font.size=Pt(9)
    # proposed addition
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); r=p.add_run('[ADD — Polaris proposal] '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=BLUE; r.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    ra=p.add_run(proposed); ra.font.color.rgb=BLUE; ra.font.underline=True; ra.font.size=Pt(9)
    # basis/risk/position table
    t=doc.add_table(rows=3, cols=2); t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER; set_table_borders(t)
    labels=['Basis / cross-reference','Risk if unchanged','Position']
    vals=[basis, risk, position]
    for i,(lab,val) in enumerate(zip(labels,vals)):
        c1,c2=t.rows[i].cells; set_cell_shading(c1,GRAY); set_cell_margins(c1); set_cell_margins(c2)
        c1.paragraphs[0].add_run(lab).bold=True; c2.paragraphs[0].add_run(val)
    # actual comment
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); rc=p.add_run(f'MARGIN COMMENT {cid}'); rc.bold=True; rc.font.color.rgb=RED; rc.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    text=f'{comment_text}' + (f'  Authority: {citations}' if citations else '')
    try:
        doc.add_comment([rc], text, author='Whitfield & Crane', initials='W&C')
    except Exception:
        pass
    t2=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1); t2.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER; set_table_borders(t2, color='C9A2A2', sz='6')
    c=t2.cell(0,0); set_cell_shading(c,PALE_RED if tier=='CRITICAL' else PALE_YELLOW); set_cell_margins(c,100,140,100,140)
    p=c.paragraphs[0]; r=p.add_run('COMMENT: '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RED
    p.add_run(text)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)

    t=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER; set_table_borders(t)
    set_repeat_table_header(t.rows[0])
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        cell=t.rows[0].cells[i]; set_cell_shading(cell,DARK); set_cell_margins(cell); p=cell.paragraphs[0]; p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER; r=p.add_run(h); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(255,255,255); r.font.size=Pt(8)
    for row in rows:
        cells=t.add_row().cells
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            set_cell_margins(cells[i]); cells[i].paragraphs[0].add_run(str(val)).font.size=Pt(8)
            if i==0: set_cell_shading(cells[i],GRAY)
    if widths: set_col_widths(t,widths)
    return t

def add_heading(doc, text, level=1):
    doc.add_paragraph(text, style=f'Heading {level}')

def add_para(doc, text, bold_prefix=None, style=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    if bold_prefix and text.startswith(bold_prefix):
        r=p.add_run(bold_prefix); r.bold=True; p.add_run(text[len(bold_prefix):])
    else: p.add_run(text)
    return p
