add_heading(red,'2. Annotated Clause-by-Clause Redline',1)
add_para(red,'The following blocks show the material draft language and the proposed seller-side replacement. Conforming provisions are addressed in the full-document disposition at the end of this markup.')

add_redline_block(red,'C-1','CRITICAL','Section 3.1 — Standard of Performance',
'“at least equal to or better than” the level provided during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to Closing, and “in all cases in accordance with industry best practices”; sufficient resources at all times.',
'Service Provider shall perform each Service in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such Service (or substantially similar service) was provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date. Historical practices, methodologies, systems and resource levels shall be the benchmark. Service Provider shall not be required to exceed that historical level, prioritize the Services over its retained businesses, or adopt external industry standards, best practices, new methodologies or systems not then used for the Business.',
'APA §§7.12(a), 7.12(f); Playbook §2.1.',
'The current standard creates an objective ratchet and an undefined external benchmark. It can require Polaris to improve service levels and prioritize Trident over retained divisions.',
'Firm must-change. “Commercially reasonable efforts” may be discussed only as a fallback after the historical benchmark is preserved.',
'Replace the 24-month lookback and “equal to or better” / best-practices language. This is a direct APA conflict and a material operational-risk issue.', 'APA §§7.12(a), 7.12(f)')

add_redline_block(red,'C-2','CRITICAL','Section 5.2 — Automatic Renewal',
'Automatic renewal for successive six-month periods, up to two Renewal Terms, unless Polaris gives non-renewal notice 120 days before expiration.',
'Delete Section 5.2 in its entirety. The Agreement and each Service shall expire no later than eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, unless the Parties mutually agree in a written amendment to extend an individual Service for no more than an additional six (6) months. No automatic renewal or extension shall apply. Any extension remains subject to the APA and the applicable cost-plus cap.',
'APA §7.12(a); Playbook §3.1.',
'As drafted, the TSA can run 30 months and renewal occurs by inaction. This deprives Polaris of an exit, reallocates resources indefinitely and conflicts with the APA hard stop.',
'Firm must-change. No automatic renewal; any extension requires mutual written agreement.',
'Delete the automatic-renewal mechanism and conform the term to the APA. Because the APA caps markups at 10%, the markup in any extension must not exceed that cap even though the playbook target is cost-plus-15% for an extension.', 'APA §7.12(a)')

add_redline_block(red,'C-3','CRITICAL','Section 5.3 — Termination of Individual Services',
'Either Party may terminate an individual Service upon not less than one hundred twenty (120) days’ prior written notice; Fees cease on the effective date.',
'Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon exactly ninety (90) days’ prior written notice. Buyer shall pay Fees accrued through the effective date and reimburse Seller for non-cancelable costs or commitments incurred before receipt of the notice in reasonable reliance on continuation of the Service, subject to commercially reasonable mitigation.',
'APA §7.12(c).',
'The 120-day period locks Polaris into service obligations longer than the APA permits and omits the express protection for non-cancelable commitments.',
'Firm must-change. The 90-day period is both the minimum and maximum under the APA.',
'Change 120 days to 90 days and restore the APA’s non-cancelable-cost reimbursement. Do not retain any longer or shorter period in a schedule.', 'APA §7.12(c)')

add_redline_block(red,'C-4','CRITICAL','Sections 6.1 and 6.4 / Schedule G — Fee methodology and true-up',
'Fees are the sole compensation and are fixed for the duration of the Term; no escalation or adjustment except as expressly provided. Schedule G fixes the monthly fees and prohibits additional charges without Buyer approval.',
'Fees are estimated monthly charges based on Fully-Loaded Cost plus a markup not exceeding 10% of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost. Fees shall be adjusted as necessary to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period, calculated consistently with the APA. No category may exceed the applicable Exhibit H estimate by more than 5% without Buyer’s prior written consent. Reasonable direct out-of-pocket and third-party costs incurred in providing the Services may be invoiced as included in, or in addition to, the estimated monthly charges to the extent consistent with the APA and applicable Schedule.',
'APA §7.12(b); APA Exhibit H; Playbook §§4.1–4.2.',
'The fixed-fee language may prevent Polaris from recovering actual cost increases and is inconsistent with the APA’s required actual-cost adjustment. The current “all-in” wording also shifts unbudgeted third-party costs to Polaris.',
'Firm on APA conformity and 10% cap; mechanics and documentation are negotiable.',
'Replace fixed-fee language with an actual-cost adjustment mechanism, while preserving the APA’s 5% estimate threshold and 10% per-category markup cap.', 'APA §7.12(b)')

add_redline_block(red,'C-5','CRITICAL','Section 10.1 — Aggregate Liability Cap',
'Polaris’s aggregate liability shall not exceed two hundred percent (200%) of total Service Charges actually paid under the Agreement as of the claim date.',
'Polaris’s aggregate liability under or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by Buyer to Seller during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date the applicable claim is first asserted in writing. During the first twelve (12) months after Closing, the cap equals the TSA Fees actually paid from Closing through the claim-assertion date. The cap applies in the aggregate and includes Polaris’s Affiliates, officers, directors, employees and agents. The carve-outs shall be limited to those required by APA §7.12(d), including fraud or willful misconduct, confidentiality breaches, and qualifying third-party indemnity claims.',
'APA §7.12(d); Playbook §5.1.',
'The draft uses a 200% total-fee cap. Using the draft’s as-written monthly total of $1,139,000, an 18-month run produces $20,502,000 of fees and a $41,004,000 cap. Correcting IT to the APA-compliant 10% markup yields $1,122,000 per month; the APA rolling 12-month cap is $13,464,000. The draft therefore creates approximately $27,540,000 of additional exposure (about 3.05x) in the full-term scenario. At month 12, the as-written draft cap would be $27,336,000 versus the $13,464,000 APA cap.',
'Firm must-change. The cap formulation is expressly mandated by the executed APA and is not a negotiation point.',
'Replace the total-fees multiple with the APA’s trailing 12-month fees-actually-paid formulation. The numeric comparison assumes all six services run for 18 months at the schedule amounts; actual exposure will vary with duration and actual costs.', 'APA §7.12(d)')

add_redline_block(red,'C-6','CRITICAL','Section 10.2 — Consequential Damages',
'“SERVICE PROVIDER HEREBY WAIVES” all consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary and indirect damages against Service Recipient.',
'NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOST PROFITS, LOST REVENUE, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, DIMINUTION IN VALUE, LOSS OF GOODWILL OR COST OF REPLACEMENT SERVICES, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF THEORY OR NOTICE OF POSSIBILITY; PROVIDED THAT THIS SENTENCE SHALL NOT LIMIT A PARTY’S LIABILITY FOR THIRD-PARTY CLAIMS FOR WHICH INDEMNIFICATION IS PROVIDED UNDER THIS AGREEMENT.',
'APA §7.12(d); Playbook §5.2.',
'The unilateral waiver leaves Polaris exposed to Trident’s claims for business interruption, lost contracts, supply-chain disruption and other consequential loss while waiving Polaris’s reciprocal claims.',
'Firm must-change. Never accept a non-mutual waiver. The third-party indemnity carve-out tracks the APA.',
'Make the waiver mutual and preserve the APA’s third-party indemnification carve-out. Any broader playbook carve-outs for confidentiality or IP should be handled consistently with the cap and APA text.', 'APA §7.12(d)')

add_redline_block(red,'C-7','CRITICAL','Section 7.1 — Service Provider Materials / IP',
'Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt and create derivative works of all Service Provider Materials, with sublicense rights surviving termination.',
'Delete the license grant. All Service Provider Materials, including tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, systems, know-how and other proprietary technology, remain Polaris’s sole and exclusive property. No license, sublicense, or other right or interest is granted. During the Term only, Trident may access Service Provider Materials solely to the extent necessary to receive the Services and may not copy, modify, reverse engineer, distribute, sublicense or create derivative works. All access ends immediately upon expiration or termination, subject only to a separately negotiated written license.',
'Playbook §6.1; client instructions from Victoria Andersen.',
'The current provision would export Polaris’s enterprise-wide operational IP across all four divisions on a perpetual, irrevocable and royalty-free basis. It creates competitive leakage and is a board-level concern.',
'Firm, non-negotiable. If Trident requires post-transition access, use a separate, priced license agreement with restrictions.',
'Delete the entire license and substitute a no-license reservation with access only during the service term.', 'Playbook §6.1')

add_redline_block(red,'C-8','CRITICAL','Sections 8.4 and new 8.5 — Mexico data privacy and IMMEX',
'Each Party shall comply only with applicable United States privacy and data-protection laws. The Schedule E IMMEX note merely states that the Parties will include “appropriate provisions.”',
'Each Party shall comply with all applicable data-protection laws, expressly including Mexico’s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (LFPDPPP) and its Regulations. For Monterrey employee data, Trident is the data controller and Polaris is the processor/service provider. The Parties shall implement or attach a data-processing addendum covering purpose limitation, documented instructions, privacy notices (avisos de privacidad), required consents or other lawful transfer mechanisms, security measures, subprocessors, breach notice to Trident without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours after awareness, assistance with data-subject requests, return/deletion and legally required retention. Trident shall be responsible for controller notices, lawful basis and employee-facing disclosures; Polaris shall process only for the Services and follow documented instructions.

New Section 8.5 — IMMEX. Trident, as the post-Closing operator of the Monterrey Facility, shall have primary responsibility for maintaining or obtaining the Facility’s IMMEX certification and complying with Mexican customs and trade requirements, including temporary-import records and Secretaría de Economía filings. Polaris shall provide the specified transition assistance and reasonably cooperate with transfer, renewal and reporting activities, but shall not be responsible for Trident’s failure to obtain or maintain post-Closing certification. Each Party shall promptly notify the other, and in any event within two Business Days, of any event that could reasonably jeopardize the certification or create a customs violation; the Parties shall cooperate on a remediation plan.',
'APA §7.12(g); Playbook §§6.3 and 12; client instructions regarding 300+ Mexican employees and IMMEX.',
'U.S.-only language leaves Polaris without contractual allocation for LFPDPPP compliance, cross-border transfers, breach response or data retention. The placeholder IMMEX language leaves unclear who maintains certification and who bears customs/tax exposure if it is jeopardized.',
'Firm must-change. Specific responsibility, notification and cooperation terms are required. Detailed local-law implementation should be confirmed by Mexico counsel, but the TSA should not be left blank.',
'Insert substantive provisions now and attach a short data-processing addendum before signing. Keep Buyer as primary operator for IMMEX after Closing and limit Polaris’s liability to its own breach / gross negligence / willful misconduct under the agreed caps.', 'APA §7.12(g)')

add_redline_block(red,'S-1','SIGNIFICANT','Section 4.3 and Schedule H — Key Personnel / staffing discretion',
'Polaris may not reassign, transfer, terminate or remove named Key Personnel without Trident’s prior written consent; replacements require Trident approval and FTE allocations are minimum commitments.',
'Polaris shall retain sole discretion over the hiring, assignment, reassignment, promotion, transfer, replacement and termination of personnel providing Services. Polaris shall maintain reasonably qualified personnel sufficient to meet the applicable Service Standard. For personnel identified on an agreed contact list, Polaris shall provide at least fifteen (15) Business Days’ advance notice of a planned reassignment or replacement where practicable and shall designate a reasonably qualified replacement, but no Trident consent shall be required. The Schedule H list and FTE percentages are planning estimates, not minimum staffing commitments.',
'Playbook §7.1; APA §7.12(e) (no obligation to maintain any employee solely for Services).',
'Buyer consent over employment decisions impairs Polaris’s ability to manage a shared-services workforce, may create employment-law complications and could force Polaris to retain personnel solely for Trident.',
'Firm target. A 15-business-day notice and qualified-replacement obligation is a reasonable fallback; buyer consent is not acceptable.',
'Remove consent rights and minimum FTE commitments. Make Schedule H a non-binding planning list.', 'Playbook §7.1')

add_redline_block(red,'S-2','SIGNIFICANT','Sections 9.1–9.2 — Indemnification',
'Polaris indemnifies Trident for any breach of any representation, warranty, covenant or obligation and any violation of Applicable Law; indemnities are not expressly limited to third-party claims or the aggregate cap.',
'Trident shall indemnify Polaris for third-party claims arising from Trident’s use of or reliance on the Services, Trident’s breach of this Agreement, or the negligent or wrongful acts of Trident or its personnel, except to the extent caused by Polaris’s gross negligence or willful misconduct. Polaris’s indemnity shall be limited to third-party claims to the extent caused by Polaris’s gross negligence or willful misconduct in performing the Services. All indemnification obligations are subject to Section 10.1, except only to the extent expressly carved out by APA §7.12(d).',
'Playbook §5.3; APA §7.12(d).',
'The draft converts ordinary contract breaches and any statutory violation into uncapped first-party indemnity claims against Polaris. It also risks making the indemnity broader than the APA’s negotiated risk allocation.',
'Firm target. Proportionate-fault language may be a fallback, but provider indemnity must remain third-party and gross-negligence / willful-misconduct based.',
'Rewrite both indemnities to address third-party claims and apply the cap. Add a direct-claim remedy under Article 10 only.', 'Playbook §5.3')

add_redline_block(red,'S-3','SIGNIFICANT','New Section 5.7 — Termination Assistance / wind-down',
'No express termination-assistance or wind-down obligation; Section 5.5 ends all rights and obligations immediately.',
'Upon expiration or termination of a Service, Polaris may provide reasonable termination assistance for up to sixty (60) days, limited to knowledge transfer, data migration support, cooperation with replacement providers and transition documentation. Such assistance shall be separately invoiced at the applicable cost-plus rate permitted by the APA and shall not be required while Trident has unpaid undisputed amounts. Polaris shall have no obligation to provide assistance beyond the stated period or to maintain personnel, systems or third-party arrangements solely for that purpose.',
'Playbook §3.4; APA §7.12(e).',
'Silence creates uncertainty and invites claims that Polaris owes indefinite post-termination cooperation. An uncapped or unpriced wind-down would extend the operational burden after the service ends.',
'Include the boundary and compensation. 60 days is the target; up to 90 days and pricing can be negotiated, but the APA markup cap remains controlling.',
'Add a defined wind-down right/obligation and condition it on payment and available resources.', 'Playbook §3.4')

add_redline_block(red,'S-4','SIGNIFICANT','New Section 2.5 — Change orders',
'No formal process for out-of-scope services, volume increases or scope modifications.',
'No out-of-scope Service, material volume increase, enhancement or change to a Service shall be performed unless documented in a written change order signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. Acceptance shall be at Polaris’s sole discretion. The change order shall state scope, assumptions, schedule, fees, applicable markup (not exceeding the APA cap unless the APA expressly permits otherwise) and any advance payment. Polaris shall have no obligation to perform until the change order is fully executed.',
'Playbook §4.4; APA §7.12(b).',
'Without a change-order gate, Trident can expand scope informally and later argue that the work is covered by the fixed monthly fee.',
'Firm on written dual signature, seller discretion and no work before execution. Pricing is subject to the APA cap; the playbook’s cost-plus-15% target cannot override the APA.',
'Insert a new Section 2.5 and cross-reference it in each Schedule’s assumptions.', 'Playbook §4.4')

add_redline_block(red,'S-5','SIGNIFICANT','Section 6.4 / Schedule G — escalation and cost recovery',
'Fees remain fixed for the Initial Term and any Renewal Terms, with no escalation or adjustment.',
'Fees may be adjusted on each anniversary of the Closing Date to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs and material cost increases resulting from a Change in Law, vendor pricing, or a material volume or scope change, in each case subject to the APA’s per-category 10% markup cap and the Exhibit H estimate / 5% consent threshold. The Parties shall use the change-order procedure for material scope or volume increases.',
'Playbook §4.2; APA §7.12(b).',
'Fixed pricing can turn the TSA into a below-market, indefinite subsidy and creates no incentive for Trident to migrate. It also may leave Polaris bearing cost inflation and vendor increases.',
'Negotiable mechanics, but Polaris must preserve actual-cost recovery and the APA cap. A CPI-only fallback is acceptable only if actual cost recovery is not impaired.',
'Replace the fixed-fee sentence and add a compliant adjustment mechanism; avoid a standalone 3% floor that could be read to violate the APA cap.', 'Playbook §4.2')

add_redline_block(red,'S-6','SIGNIFICANT','Section 6.3 — Payment terms',
'Buyer shall pay undisputed invoices within a “commercially reasonable time.”',
'Buyer shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after receipt. Any late amount shall bear interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by law. Buyer shall pay undisputed portions regardless of any dispute concerning another portion. Polaris may suspend the affected Service after an undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than sixty (60) days after written notice, without waiving any other remedy.',
'Playbook §4.3.',
'Vague timing undermines cash-flow predictability and makes non-payment difficult to enforce. The draft also lacks a suspension right for prolonged non-payment.',
'Firm target; Net 45 is the maximum fallback. Suspension after 60 days is a reasonable protection.',
'Replace “commercially reasonable time” with Net 30, add late interest, and add suspension / termination protection.', 'Playbook §4.3')

add_redline_block(red,'S-7','SIGNIFICANT','Section 14 — Audit rights',
'Trident may audit up to twice per calendar year, at Polaris’s expense, on 10 Business Days’ notice, including systems, facilities, personnel and performance records.',
'Trident may audit Polaris’s fee-related books and records no more than once in any twelve-month period, at Trident’s sole expense, on at least thirty (30) Business Days’ prior written notice. Audits shall be during normal business hours, shall not access proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies or unrelated personnel records, and shall be conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality. If an audit shows an overcharge exceeding 5% for the audited period, Polaris shall credit the overcharge and reasonable audit costs; otherwise Trident bears all audit costs. Audit results are confidential.',
'Playbook §9; APA §7.12(b) cost methodology.',
'The draft invites disruptive and potentially frivolous audits, shifts all cost to Polaris and exposes enterprise systems and personnel information beyond fee verification.',
'Firm target; accept twice per TSA term and 20 Business Days’ notice only as a fallback. Buyer expense and scope limits are firm.',
'Replace the broad audit clause with a fee-records-only, buyer-paid regime and a 5% threshold.', 'Playbook §9')

add_redline_block(red,'S-8','SIGNIFICANT','Section 12.1 — Force majeure exit',
'Force majeure suspends performance and requires mitigation, but contains no termination trigger for a prolonged event.',
'If a Force Majeure Event materially prevents performance of an affected Service for ninety (90) consecutive days, either Party may terminate the affected Service on written notice without further liability for nonperformance after the termination date. Fees shall be equitably adjusted to reflect services actually delivered. Accrued payment obligations and amounts due for completed Services survive.',
'Playbook §10; standard seller-side wind-down protection.',
'Without an exit right, Polaris can remain tied to an unavailable or obsolete service indefinitely and may face disputes over when performance must resume.',
'Firm target; 120 consecutive days is the maximum fallback.',
'Add the 90-day termination trigger and clarify payment / adjustment mechanics.', 'Playbook §10')

add_redline_block(red,'S-9','SIGNIFICANT','Section 13 — insurance',
'Trident maintains only $2M CGL; Polaris maintains $5M CGL, workers’ compensation and $5M E&O for 12 months after termination; no additional-insured or waiver-of-subrogation protection.',
'Trident shall maintain through the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter: (i) CGL of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence and aggregate; (ii) umbrella/excess liability of at least $5,000,000; and (iii) workers’ compensation at statutory limits. Polaris shall be named as additional insured under the CGL and umbrella policies, with waiver of subrogation in Polaris’s favor; certificates are due within 10 Business Days after Closing and annually thereafter. Polaris shall maintain only the insurance it customarily maintains for comparable operations and coverage required by law, with no obligation to procure additional or extended post-Term coverage solely for the TSA.',
'Playbook §8; industrial / chemical manufacturing risk.',
'The buyer’s $2M-only requirement is inadequate for a coatings/manufacturing operation and gives Polaris no direct policy rights. The draft simultaneously imposes unnecessary additional insurance burdens on Polaris.',
'$5M limits are the target; $3M CGL / umbrella is the minimum fallback. Additional insured and waiver of subrogation are firm. Seller coverage language is negotiable but should not require incremental procurement.',
'Upgrade Trident’s coverage and reduce Polaris’s affirmative procurement burden.', 'Playbook §8')

add_redline_block(red,'S-10','SIGNIFICANT','Sections 15.1–15.2 — law and dispute resolution',
'Ohio law; exclusive litigation in Cuyahoga County, Ohio; jury waiver.',
'Pennsylvania law governs. Disputes shall first be escalated to CFO/General Counsel-level representatives for fifteen (15) Business Days, followed by optional non-binding mediation. Any unresolved dispute shall be finally resolved by confidential binding arbitration administered by the AAA under its Commercial Arbitration Rules before one arbitrator in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The arbitrator may award all remedies available under the Agreement, subject to its limitations; judgment may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction.',
'Playbook §11; Polaris headquarters and service personnel are in Pittsburgh.',
'Buyer-home-state litigation creates home-court and public-docket risk, increases discovery burden and loses the confidentiality and industry expertise advantages of arbitration.',
'Pennsylvania / AAA / Pittsburgh is the target. A neutral arbitration location or three arbitrators for disputes above $5M may be considered as a fallback; litigation is not preferred.',
'Replace Ohio law and court litigation with Pennsylvania law and the three-step arbitration process.', 'Playbook §11')

add_redline_block(red,'S-11','SIGNIFICANT','New Section 15.12 — non-solicitation',
'No restriction on Trident soliciting or hiring Polaris service personnel.',
'During the Term and for twelve (12) months after expiration or termination, Trident shall not, without Polaris’s prior written consent, solicit, recruit, hire or engage any employee of Polaris or its Affiliates who provided Services. This does not prohibit general solicitations not targeted at Polaris personnel or hiring an individual terminated by Polaris without cause. The Parties acknowledge the covenant is intended to protect continuity of the Services and Polaris’s shared-services workforce.',
'Playbook §7.2; client instruction to identify missing standard playbook provisions.',
'Trident can cherry-pick personnel who gain deep knowledge of Polaris’s systems and processes, depleting the workforce and undermining delivery to remaining Polaris businesses.',
'Firm target; six months post-termination is the absolute minimum fallback. Scope should cover all service-providing employees, not only named Key Personnel.',
'Add the covenant before the miscellaneous provisions / signature page.', 'Playbook §7.2')

add_redline_block(red,'M-1','MINOR','Section 15.3 — notices',
'Email notice is effective only if a copy is also sent by overnight courier the same day; provision otherwise differs from APA §12.1.',
'Notices are effective upon receipt by hand or overnight courier, or on the date sent by email with confirmation of transmission if sent during the recipient’s normal business hours (and the next Business Day if sent after hours), or on the third Business Day after certified mail. Notices for Section 5.3 termination shall use these mechanics.',
'APA §12.1; Playbook §13.3.',
'Mismatched notice mechanics can create disputes over the effective date of a 90-day service termination notice or other deadline-sensitive notice.',
'Cleanup / conforming change.',
'Align the TSA notice clause with the executed APA and delete the same-day courier requirement for email.', 'APA §12.1')

add_redline_block(red,'M-2','MINOR','Section 11.2 — provider representations',
'Polaris represents it has personnel, systems, facilities and capabilities “necessary and sufficient” and that Services will be performed in compliance with all Applicable Laws.',
'As of the Effective Date, and subject to the scope limitations, exclusions, historical Service Standard and cooperation obligations in this Agreement, Polaris represents only that it has personnel, systems and facilities reasonably available to perform the Services as described in the Schedules. Polaris shall perform the Services in compliance with Applicable Law to the extent applicable to Polaris’s performance and within the agreed scope. No representation is made regarding outcomes, business results or Buyer’s compliance obligations.',
'Playbook service-standard and scope principles; §2.2 / §3.2.',
'Absolute “necessary and sufficient” and all-laws language may create a warranty exceeding the historical standard and may make Polaris responsible for Trident’s own regulatory obligations.',
'Negotiable qualification; preserve the disclaimer and no-results language.',
'Narrow the representation to available resources, agreed scope and laws applicable to Polaris’s performance.', 'Playbook §§2.1–2.2')

add_redline_block(red,'M-3','MINOR','Schedule B / Section 3.1 — “industry-standard” overlays',
'Schedule B requires cybersecurity monitoring consistent with “industry-standard practices”; Section 3.1 imposes industry best practices across all Services.',
'Cybersecurity monitoring shall be consistent with Polaris’s protocols and security controls used for its own businesses during the twelve (12) months preceding Closing, subject to reasonable changes applied across Polaris’s enterprise. No external “industry standard,” “best practice,” or professional-services benchmark shall apply unless expressly agreed in a signed change order.',
'Playbook §2.1; APA §7.12(f).',
'External standards are undefined, potentially expensive and could impose a higher standard than Polaris used for the Business.',
'Firm principle; reasonable security updates applied enterprise-wide are acceptable.',
'Conform Schedule B to the historical benchmark and enterprise-wide change concept.', 'APA §7.12(f)')

add_redline_block(red,'M-4','MINOR','Schedule H — personnel list and FTEs',
'Schedule H names fourteen individuals, sets minimum FTE allocations and makes any reduction subject to buyer consent.',
'Delete the named-person and minimum-FTE requirements. If the Parties retain Schedule H, it shall identify illustrative contacts and anticipated allocation ranges for planning only; all assignments remain subject to Section 4.3 and Polaris’s sole discretion. Polaris may update the list by notice without amendment.',
'Playbook §7.1; APA Exhibit H expressly treats FTE counts as estimates adjustable in Seller’s reasonable discretion.',
'Named individuals and minimum allocations conflict with the APA Exhibit H framework and constrain Polaris’s ability to manage shared personnel.',
'Cleanup with room to agree on a non-binding contact list.',

def shade(cell,fill):
p=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); x=p.find(qn('w:shd'))
if x is None: x=OxmlElement('w:shd'); p.append(x)
x.set(qn('w:fill'),fill)
def border(cell,color='B7C9D6',sz='6'):
p=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); b=p.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
if b is None: b=OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); p.append(b)
for e in ('top','left','bottom','right'):
x=b.find(qn('w:'+e))
if x is None: x=OxmlElement('w:'+e); b.append(x)
x.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); x.set(qn('w:sz'),sz); x.set(qn('w:color'),color)
def margins(cell):
p=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); m=p.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')

39:We reviewed Trident's April 28, 2025 draft TSA against the Polaris TSA Playbook (January 15, 2025) and the TSA-relevant provisions of the executed APA, including §7.12 and Exhibit H. The draft is not ready to circulate without material revision. Eight issues are Critical because they directly conflict with the APA or create unacceptable IP / cross-border risk: the service standard, term / renewal mechanics, termination notice, fee methodology and IT markup, liability cap, one-way damages waiver, perpetual IP license, and Mexico privacy / IMMEX omissions.
48:       Liability cap      As drafted: 200% of total fees. Using \$1,139,000 monthly total, 18 months = \$20,502,000 and 200% = \$41,004,000. Corrected IT at 10% gives \$1,122,000 monthly; APA rolling 12-month cap = \$13,464,000. Full-term delta = \$27,540,000 (about 3.05x).   CRITICAL / must change
50:            IP            Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to Polaris tools, methodologies, templates, software and know-how, including derivative works and sublicensing.                                                                                    CRITICAL / board-level leakage risk
52:          Mexico          U.S.-only privacy language; no LFPDPPP processing terms and no clear IMMEX owner, cost, notice or remediation allocation. Approximately 300+ Mexican employees are in scope.                                                                               CRITICAL / closing and operational risk
55:# Priority Tier 1 --- CRITICAL / APA Conflicts and Non-Negotiables
74:           C-8 --- Mexico data and IMMEX          U.S.-only privacy language; IMMEX is only a placeholder. Add LFPDPPP controller / processor terms, privacy notices, transfer mechanisms, security, breach notice and return / deletion; make Trident primary post-Closing IMMEX operator and add notice / remediation.   Firm / closing-sensitive; confirm implementation with Mexico counsel.

151:- For Mexico, offer a short-form processing addendum reviewed by Mexico counsel, but do not accept generic "comply with law" language or an IMMEX placeholder. Trident should be primary operator after Closing; Polaris can offer reasonable transition support.
161:- Ask Mexico / Latin America counsel to validate the LFPDPPP addendum, privacy notice / consent language and IMMEX allocation.
170:  **BOTTOM LINE:** The current draft shifts substantial operational and legal risk to Polaris while weakening the APA's negotiated guardrails.
